notes.1: (sn): In ancient Judaism Ezra and Nehemiah were regarded as a single book with dual authorship. According to the Talmud, “Ezra wrote his book” (b. Bava Batra 15a). The Gemara then asks and answers, “And who finished it? Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah.” Accordingly, the two are joined in the Leningrad Codex (ca. A.D. 1008), the manuscript upon which modern printed editions of the Hebrew Bible (e.g., BHK and BHS) are based.
notes.2: (sn): The name Nehemiah in Hebrew (נְחֶמְיָה, n�khemyah) means “the LORD comforts.”
notes.3: (tn): That is, the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes’ reign (cf. 2:1).

rashi.heb:
*דברי נחמיה וגו'.* 
מכאן ואילך כתב נחמיה ספר זה:
rashi.eng: *The words of Nehemiah, etc..* Nehemiah wrote this book from here on.

rashi.heb:
*שנת עשרים.* 
היא שנת עשרים לדריוש המלך שהוא ארתחששתא ובמסכת ר"ה מצאנו שנת עשרים שנת עשרים לג"ש מן הכתוב שנ' למטה ויהי בחדש ניסן שנת כ' לארתחששתא וגו' ומחדש תשרי היו מונין לחשבון השנים ועל כן נאמר כאן ויהי בחדש כסלו שנת כ' וגו' והוא כסלו הבא לאחר תשרי ולמטה נאמר ויהי בחדש ניסן שנת כ' וגומר הוא ניסן שבאותה שנה ואיני יכול לפתור ולומר מניסן היו מונין לחשבון שנותיהם ואותו מעשה הכתוב למטה שנאמר ויהי בחדש ניסן וגו' היה קודם מעשה זה שנאמר ויהי בחדש כסליו שנת כ' וגו' ואין מוקדם ומאוח' בהם דבר זה איני יכול לפתור ולומר והפרשיות מוכיחות שאף אותו מעשה של פרשה שנייה לא היתה כי אם בשביל מעשה זה של פרשה זאת ראשונה:
rashi.eng: *the twentieth year.* This refers to the twentieth year of King Darius, who is identical with Artaxerxes. In Tractate Rosh Hashanah (3a, b), we find that the phrase “the twentieth year” is mentioned twice using similar wording [to teach us that it is speaking of the identical year]. It states below (2:1), “And it came to pass in the month of Nissan of the twentieth year of Artaxerxes, etc.” The years were calculated from the month of Tishrei. It says here, “And it was in the month of Kislev of the twentieth year, etc.” This refers to the Kislev coming after Tishrei. Further down it says (2:1), “And it was in the month of Nissan of the twentieth year, etc.” This refers to the Nissan of the same year. And I cannot explain that they calculated their years from the month of Nissan and that the incident mentioned below: “And it was in the month of Nissan, etc.” occurred before this incident: “And it was in the month of Kislev, etc.” It is true that events [in the Torah] are not necessarily recorded in chronological order. Nevertheless, the chapters indicate that the second chapter took place only because of the events of the first chapter.

notes.6: (tn): The Hebrew text does not include the words “to me”; these words were supplied in the translation for the sake of clarity.
notes.7: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*אחד מאחי.* 
אחד מחברי:
rashi.eng: *one of my brethren.* one of my companions.

rashi.heb:
*ואשאלם על היהודים וגו'.* 
שאלתי להם על ענין פליטת היהודים אשר נשארו בירושלים מן השבי של בבל:
rashi.eng: *and I asked them about the Jews.* I asked them about the Jews who had escaped the Babylonian captivity and remained in Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*הפליטה.* 
על שם שנצולו מגלות בבל:
rashi.eng: *who had escaped.* because they were saved from the Babylonian exile.

rashi.heb:
*ועל ירושלים.* 
ועל ענין העיר שאלתי אליהם:
rashi.eng: *and about Jerusalem.* And I asked them about the city.

notes.9: (tn, Heb): “have been burned with fire” (so also in Neh 2:17). The expression “burned with fire” is redundant in contemporary English; the translation uses “burned down” for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמרו לי.* 
השיבו לי על ראשון ראשון ועל אחרון אחרון תחלה על ענין היהודים ואח"כ על ענין החומות והשערים:
rashi.eng: *And they said to me.* They answered my first question first and my latter question last; first, concerning the Jews and afterwards, concerning the wall and the gates.

rashi.heb:
*הנשארים וגו'.* 
אותם היהודים אשר נשארו שם במדינת ירושלים הם נתונים ברעה גדולה ובחרפ' לפי שהעובדי כוכבים בוזזים ושוללים אותם:
rashi.eng: *who remained.* Those Jews who remained in the province of Jerusalem are in great trouble and reproach because the gentiles plunder and pillage them.

rashi.heb:
*וחומת ירושלים מפורצת.* 
וחומת העיר הרי היא פרוצה והשערים שרופים באש כקדמתן שישראל לא בנו חומות העיר ושעריה כי אם בנין ב"ה לבדו:
rashi.eng: *and the wall of Jerusalem is breached.* And the wall of the city is breached, and the gates are burned with fire as they were before, for Israel had not built the wall of the city or its gates, only the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*נצתו.* 
כמו נוצתו (ס"א נצתו כמו נתצו):
rashi.eng: *were burned.* Heb. נִצְתוּ, like נֻצְתוּ.

notes.10: (tn, Heb): “sat down.” Context suggests that this was a rather sudden action, resulting from the emotional shock of the unpleasant news, so “abruptly” has been supplied in the present translation.

rashi.heb:
*ימים.* 
כמה ימים:
rashi.eng: *for days.* Heb. יָמִים, many days.

notes.11: (tn, Heb): “the covenant and loyal love.” The phrase is a hendiadys: the first noun retains its full nominal sense, while the second noun functions adjectivally (“loyal love” = loving). Alternately, the first might function adjectivally and the second noun function as the noun: “covenant and loyal love” = covenant fidelity (see Neh 9:32).
notes.12: (tn, Heb): “keep.” The Hebrew verb שָׁמַר (shamar, “to observe; to keep”) is often used as an idiom that means “to obey” the commandments of God (e.g., Exod 20:6; Deut 5:16; 23:24; 29:8; Judg 2:22; 1 Kgs 2:43; 11:11; Ps 119:8, 17, 34; Jer 35:18; Ezek 17:14; Amos 2:4). See BDB 1036 s.v. 3.c.

rashi.heb:
*אנא.* 
לשון בקשה ותחנה:
rashi.eng: *I beseech You.* Heb. אָנָא, an expression of request and supplication.

notes.13: (tn, Heb): “have sinned.” For stylistic reasons – to avoid redundancy in English – this was translated as “committed.”

rashi.heb:
*קשבת.* 
כמו קושבת כו' כאשר יאמר מאהב אוהב כן יאמר מן קשב קושב וקושבת:
rashi.eng: *attentive.* Heb. קַשֶּׁבֶת, like קוֹשֶּׁבֶת, listening, for just as one says from אוֹהֵב, אָהַב, so does one say from קָשַּׁב, קוֹשֵּׁב and קוֹשֶּׁבֶת.

rashi.heb:
*חבול.* 
שם דבר לשון השחתה וחי"ת ננקדה בחטף פתח ואיני יכול לפותרו בל' פעול שא"כ היה לו לנקד חי"ת בקמץ גדול:
rashi.eng: *We have dealt corruptly.* Heb. חֲבֹל, a noun, an expression of corruption, since the “heth” is vowelized with a “hataf pattah,” and I cannot interpret it as a verb form, because in that case, it would have to be vowelized with a large “kamatz.”

rashi.heb:
*חבלנו.* 
לשון השחתה כמו (בדניאל ו׳:כ״ג) חבולא לא עבדת וכן חברו מנחם:
rashi.eng: *we have dealt corruptly.* Heb. חָבַלְנוּ, an expression of corruption, as in Daniel (6:23): “I have done no harm.”

notes.17: (tn, Heb): “keep.” See the note on the word “obey” in Neh 1:5.
notes.18: (tn, Heb): “at the end of the heavens.”

rashi.heb:
*אם יהיה נדחכם.* 
כענין שנאמר אם יהיה נדחך וגו' (דברים ל׳:ד׳):
rashi.eng: *if your exile is.* like the matter that is stated (Deut. 30:4): “If your exile is at the end of the heavens, etc.”

notes.19: (tn): The interjection אָנָּא (’anna’) is an emphatic term of entreaty: “please!” (BDB 58 s.v.; HALOT 69-70 s.v.). This term is normally reserved for pleas for mercy from God in life-and-death situations (2 Kgs 20:3 = Isa 38:3; Pss 116:4; 118:25; Jonah 1:14; 4:2) and for forgiveness of heinous sins that would result or have resulted in severe judgment from God (Exod 32:31; Dan 9:4; Neh 1:5, 11).
notes.22: (tn, Heb): “grant compassion.” The words “to me” are supplied in the translation for the sake of smoothness and style in English.
notes.23: (tn): The vav (ו) on וַאֲנִי (va’ani, “Now, I”) introduces a disjunctive parenthetical clause that provides background information to the reader.

rashi.heb:
*אנא אדני תהי נא אזנך קשבת.* 
בתחלת תפלתו אמר לשון זה של תחנה וכן לאחר תפלתו:
rashi.eng: *I beseech You, O Lord, may Your ear now be attentive.* At the beginning of his prayer he used this expression, and so after his prayer.

rashi.heb:
*לעבדך היום וגו'.* 
כך היה מתפלל על עצמו:
rashi.eng: *Your servant.* This is what he prayed for himself.

rashi.heb:
*לפני האיש הזה.* 
לפני המלך:
rashi.eng: *before this man.* before the king.

rashi.heb:
*משקה.* 
כמו (ראשית מ') משקה למלך מצרים וזה שפירשתי למעלה (עזרא ב') כדברי רבותינו התרשתא הוא נחמיה:
rashi.eng: *butler.* Heb. מַשְּׁקֶה, like (Gen. 40:1): “… the butler of (מַשְּׁקֶה) the king of Egypt.” This is what I explained above (Ezra 2:63) according to the words of our Sages, that Hattirshatha is Nehemiah.

notes.24: (tc): The translation reads with the LXX וְיַיִן לְפָנַי (v�yayin l�fanay, “and wine before me”) rather than יַיִן לְפָנָיו (yayin l�fanayv, “wine before him”) of the MT. The initial vav (ו) on original וְיַיִן probably dropped out due to haplograpy or orthographic confusion with the two yods (י) which follow. The final vav on לְפָנָיו in the MT was probably added due to dittography with the vav on the immediately following word.
notes.25: (tc): The translation reads לְפָנֵים (l�fanim, “formerly”) rather than לְפָנָיו (l�fanayv, “to his face”) of the MT. The MT seems to suggest that Nehemiah was not sad before the king, which is contrary to what follows.
notes.26: (tn): Or “showed him a sullen face.” See HALOT 1251 s.v. רַע, רָע 9.
notes.27: (tn): This expression is either to be inferred from the context, or perhaps one should read לְפָנָיו (l�fanayv, “before him”; cf. the MT) in addition to לְפָנִים (l�fanim, “formerly”). See preceding note on the word “previously.”

rashi.heb:
*לארתחשסתא.* 
הוא דריוש ועל שם המלכות נקרא כך:
rashi.eng: *of… Artaxerxes.* That was Darius, and because of his kingship he was called this.

rashi.heb:
*יין לפניו.* 
הביאו יין לפני המלך בחצר:
rashi.eng: *wine before him.* They brought wine before the king in the court.

rashi.heb:
*ואשא את היין.* 
ואנכי נשאתי את כוס היין ונתתיה למלך וכך הוא המנהג שהמביא יין בחצר המלך אינו נושא ונותנו למלך אבל שר המשקים מקבל כוס היין מיד המביא והוא נושא ונותנו למלך:
rashi.eng: *and I carried the wine.* And I carried the cup of wine and gave it to the king, and so is the custom, that the one who brings wine into the king’s court does not carry it and give it to the king, but the chief butler receives it from the hand of the one who brings it, and carries it and gives it to the king.

rashi.heb:
*לא הייתי רע לפניו.* 
ואני לא הייתי רגיל להיות רע לפניו ברוע פנים כי אם שמח וטוב לב ועתה הייתי זועף ברוע פנים:
rashi.eng: *And I had never been sad in his presence.* And I was not accustomed to being sad in his presence, to have a sad face, but to be happy and cheerful, but now I was sad with a sad face.

rashi.heb:
*ואתה אינך חולה.* 
והרי אין אתה חולה:
rashi.eng: *You are not ill.* Is it not so that you are not ill?

rashi.heb:
*אין זה.* 
אין המעשה הזה כי אם רוע לב שיש בלבבך עלי להמיתני בסם המות בשתיית כוס זה:
rashi.eng: *This is nothing.* This incident is only wickedness of heart, that you have in your heart to put me to death by poisoning this cup.

rashi.heb:
*ואירא הרבה מאד.* 
ונתיראתי מאד על כך שלא יעליל עלי המלך עלילה:
rashi.eng: *And I became very frightened.* And I became very frightened about this, lest the king accuse me falsely.

rashi.heb:
*מדוע לא ירעו פני.* 
מדוע לא יהיו פני רעים:
rashi.eng: *Why should my countenance not be sad.* [as translated,] why should my countenance not be sad.

rashi.heb:
*שר העיר.* 
ירושלים שהיא בית קברות אבותי חרבה:
rashi.eng: *when the city.* Jerusalem, which is the place of the graves of my forefathers, is laid waste.

rashi.heb:
*על מה זה אתה מבקש.* 
אי זה דבר תבקש ממני ואעשה לך:
rashi.eng: *For what do you make request.* What do you request of me and I shall do it for you.

rashi.heb:
*ואתפלל.* 
ואמרתי לפני המלך בתפילתי כן יהיה רצון מלפני אלהי השמים שתמלא שאלתי ובקשתי:
rashi.eng: *And I prayed.* And I said before the king in my prayer, “May it be Your will, O God of the heavens, that You fulfill my petition and my request.”

notes.31: (tn, Heb): “If upon the king it is good.” So also in v. 7.

rashi.heb:
*אשר תשלחני.* 
שתתן לי רשות לעלות לירושלים ולבנותה:
rashi.eng: *that you send me.* that you grant me permission to ascend to Jerusalem and build it.

notes.32: (tn): Or “queen,” so most English versions (cf. HALOT 1415 s.v. שֵׁגַל); TEV “empress.”
notes.33: (tn, Heb): “It was good before the king and he sent me.”

rashi.heb:
*ויאמר לי המלך.* 
בשעה שדבר אלי המלך היתה אשתו המלכה יושבת אצלו:
rashi.eng: *And the king said to me.* At the time the king spoke to me, his wife, the queen, was sitting beside him.

rashi.heb:
*והשגל.* 
אשתו המלכה כענין שנאמר (דניאל ה') שגלתיה ולחנתיה, שכן נוהג המקרא לכתוב המלכה אצל הפלגש נשיו ופלגשיו כמו מלכות ופלגשים (שיר /השירים/ ו'):
rashi.eng: *and the queen.* Heb. וְהַשֵּׁגָל, his wife the queen, as it is stated (Dan. 5:2): “… his queen (שֵּׁגְלָתֵהּ) and his concubine,” for it is customary for Scripture to write “the queen,” next to “the concubine;” his wives and his concubines, like (Song 6:9): “ וּפִּילַגְשִּׁים מְלָכוֹת, queens and concubines.”

rashi.heb:
*עד מתי יהיה מהלכך.* 
מתי תרצה שיהא מהלכך ומסעך:
rashi.eng: *How long will your trip take.* When is it your intention to return?

rashi.heb:
*ומתי תשוב.* 
ומתי דעתך לחזור:
rashi.eng: *and when will you return?.* When is it your intention to return?

rashi.heb:
*ישלחני.* 
נתן לי רשות ללכת:
rashi.eng: *and he sent me.* He gave me permission to go.

rashi.heb:
*ואתנה לו זמן.* 
נתתי לו זמן לחזור:
rashi.eng: *and I gave him a time.* I gave him a time of return.

notes.34: (tn, Heb): “across the river,” here and often elsewhere in the Book of Nehemiah.

rashi.heb:
*אגרות יתנו לי.* 
סופריך על רשותך ודעתך חתומות בחותמך על פחות עבר הנהר של צד ארץ ישראל:
rashi.eng: *may letters be given to me.* [Let] your scribes [give me letters] by your sanction and your knowledge, sealed with your signet to the governors of the land beyond the river, on the side of the land of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*אשר יעבירוני.* 
ויתיירוני לשלום:
rashi.eng: *that they escort me through.* and escort me in peace.

rashi.heb:
*עד אשר אבוא.* 
לירושלים אשר במדינת יהודה:
rashi.eng: *until I come.* to Jerusalem, which is in the province of Judea.

notes.36: (tc): One medieval Hebrew MS, the Syriac Peshitta, Vulgate, and the Arabic read here the plural וּלְחוֹמוֹת (ul�khomot, “walls”) against the singular וּלְחוֹמַת (ul�khomat) in the MT. The plural holem vav (וֹ) might have dropped out due to dittography or the plural form might have been written defectively.
notes.37: (tn): The Hebrew text does not include the expression “these requests,” but it is implied.

rashi.heb:
*ואגרת אל אסף.* 
ותשלח כתב אגרת אל אסף:
rashi.eng: *And a letter to Asaph.* and that you send a letter to Asaph.

rashi.heb:
*שומר הפרדס.* 
ממונה היה על היערים אשר למלך:
rashi.eng: *the guardian of the king’s orchard.* He was appointed over the king’s forests.

rashi.heb:
*לקרות.* 
משקל חזק לעשות תקרות וקורות לשערי בירות הר הבית שהרי ב"ה בנו בבנינו אבל שערי חומות הר הבית וחומת החצר אשר סביב ב"ה לא בנו עדיין:
rashi.eng: *to make beams.* This is the intensive conjugation: to make ceilings and beams for the gates of the castles of the Temple Mount, for they had built the Temple as it should be built, but the gates of the walls of the Temple Mount and the wall for the court surrounding the Temple had not yet been built.

rashi.heb:
*ולחומת העיר.* 
ולעשות קורות לחומת העיר:
rashi.eng: *and for the wall of the city.* and to make beams for the wall of the city.

rashi.heb:
*ולבית אשר אבא אליו.* 
ולעשות בית אשר אשב בו לצורכי:
rashi.eng: *and for the house to which I shall go.* and to make a house in which I shall dwell for my needs.

rashi.heb:
*ויתן לי המלך.* 
את כל אשר שאלתי ממנו:
rashi.eng: *and the king gave me.* all I asked him for.

rashi.heb:
*כיד.* 
כפי ידו של הקב"ה שהיתה טובה עלי להצליחני:
rashi.eng: *according to the good hand.* according to the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, which was good upon me, to cause me to succeed.

rashi.heb:
*ואתנה להם את אגרות המלך.* 
למען יתיירוני לשלום:
rashi.eng: *and I gave them the king’s letters.* in order that they escort me in peace.

rashi.heb:
*שרי חיל ופרשים.* 
שלח המלך עמי לכבודי למען אלך לשלום:
rashi.eng: *officers of the army and horsemen.* the king sent with me [officers] in my honor, in order that I go in peace.

notes.38: (tn, Heb): “servant” (so KJV, ASV; NAB “slave”; NCV “officer.” This phrase also occurs in v. 19.

rashi.heb:
*וישמע סנבלט וגו'.* 
כאשר שמעו שבאתי לבקש טובה על ישראל ולבנות חומות ירושלים וירע בעיניהם כי היו צרי יהודה ובנימין:
rashi.eng: *Now Sanballat etc., heard.* When they heard that I had come to request good for Israel and to build the walls of Jerusalem it displeased them greatly, for they were the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin.

notes.39: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*ואהי שם ימים שלשה.* 
הייתי בירושלים ימים שלשה ולסוף שלשת ימים קמתי בלילה אני ואנשים מועטים עמי ולא הגדתי לשום אדם את אשר נתן הקב"ה בלבי:
rashi.eng: *and I was there for three days.* I was in Jerusalem for three days, and at the end of three days, I and a few men with me arose at night, and I did not tell any person what the Holy One, blessed be He, had put into my heart.

rashi.heb:
*ובהמה אין עמי.* 
כי כל האנשים מועטים אשר עמי הלכו ברגליהם אבל אני לבדי הייתי רוכב על בהמה שלא היו רוצים לרכוב על סוסיהם למען יהיו יוצאים מן העיר בצינעא בלא ידיעת אדם והם הלכו לשבור ולהפיל חומות העיר בלילה ולהרבות פרצותיה למען יהיו בני העיר למחר להוטי' ומסכימים בעצה אחת עם נחמיה לבנות חומות העיר, וכן מוכיח המעשה בתוך הפרשה:
rashi.eng: *and there were no animals with me.* The few men who were with me went by foot and I alone rode on an animal. They did not ride their horses because they wanted to leave the city in secret, without anyone knowing. They went to break and cast down the walls of the city at night and to increase their breaches in order that on the morrow, the people of the city would be eager and agree unanimously with Nehemiah to build the walls of the city. So it appears from the text.

notes.41: (tn): Or “Well of the Serpents”; or “Well of the Jackals” (cf. ASV, NIV, NLT).
notes.42: (tn): Or “Rubbish Gate” (so TEV); NASB “Refuse Gate”; NCV “Trash Gate”; CEV “Garbage Gate.”
notes.43: (tc): For the MT reading שֹׂבֵר (sover, “inspecting”) the LXX erroneously has שֹׁבֵר (shover, “breaking”). However, further destruction of Jerusalem’s walls was obviously not a part of Nehemiah’s purpose.

rashi.heb:
*ואצאה בשער הגיא.* 
יצאתי באותו שער בלילה עם האנשים אשר עמי לצד אותו מקום של עין התנין ולאותו שער האשפות שבחומות העיר והייתי פורץ בחומה והחומה היתה נוחה להפילה ולפרוץ בה לפי שהיתה שרופה באש:
rashi.eng: *And I went out through the Gate of the Valley.* I went out through that gate at night with the men who were with me toward En Hattannin and the Dung Gate in the wall of the city; and I broke the wall, and the wall was easily cast down and broken because it had been burned with fire.

rashi.heb:
*אשר הם פרוצים.* 
שהם אותם מקומו' שהיו פרוצים והם פרצו בהם יותר:
rashi.eng: *which were breached.* which are those places that were breached, and they breached them more.

rashi.heb:
*ואעבור אל שער העין.* 
ורציתי לעבור אל אותן מקומות שבחומת העיר ובאותן פרצות ואין מקום באותן פרצות לעבור ביניהם רוכב על הבהמות שהיו פרצות קטנות:
rashi.eng: *And I passed to the Fountain Gate.* And I wished to pass to those places in the wall of the city and in those breaches, and there was no place in those breaches for riders on animals to pass through because they were so small.

rashi.heb:
*ואהי עולה.* 
והייתי עולה מצד אחד בלילה והייתי שובר בחומה עם האנשים אשר עמי:
rashi.eng: *And I ascended.* And I was ascending from one side at night, and I was breaking the wall with the men who were with me.

rashi.heb:
*ואשוב ואבוא.* 
וכאשר חזרתי באתי דרך שער הגיא:
rashi.eng: *and I returned and came.* And when I returned, I came by way of the Gate of the Valley.

rashi.heb:
*והסגנים.* 
אשר בעיר לא היו יודעין להיכן הלכתי ואת המעשה אשר עשיתי:
rashi.eng: *And the prefects.* who were in the city did not know where I had gone to and what I had done.

rashi.heb:
*עד כן.* 
עד עתה:
rashi.eng: *yet.* Heb. כֵּן עַד, until now.

rashi.heb:
*ואומר אליהם.* 
למחר אמרתי להם:
rashi.eng: *And I said to them.* On the morrow I said to them.

rashi.heb:
*ולא נהיה עוד חרפה.* 
שלא יהיו צרינו בוזזים ושוללים אותנו:
rashi.eng: *and we shall no longer be a reproach.* that our adversaries should not plunder and pillage us.

notes.44: (tn, Heb): “the words of the king which he had spoken to me.”

rashi.heb:
*את יד אלהי.* 
אשר נתן לי חן והצלחה לפני המלך:
rashi.eng: *the hand of my God.* who gave me favor and success before the king.

rashi.heb:
*לטובה.* 
הכל נתכונו לטובה לבנות חומת העיר ומגדליה:
rashi.eng: *for good.* They intended everything for good-to build the wall of the city and its towers.

notes.47: (tn): The Hebrew text does not include the words “all this,” but they have been added in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וילעיגו.* 
כאשר שמעו הצרים שמועת בנין חומת העיר היו מלעיגים עלינו:
rashi.eng: *and they mocked.* When our adversaries heard the news of the building of the walls of the city, they mocked us.

rashi.heb:
*העל המלך.* 
אם על המלך אתם מורדים לבנות חומת העיר כדי למרוד בו:
rashi.eng: *are… against the king.* Are you rebelling against the king by building the wall of the city in order to rebel against him?

notes.48: (tn, Heb): “will arise and build.” The idiom “arise and…” means to begin the action described by the second verb.
notes.49: (tn, Heb): “portion or right or remembrance.” The expression is probably a hendiatris: The first two nouns retain their full nominal function, while the third noun functions adjectivally (“right or remembrance” = “ancient right”).

rashi.heb:
*ולכם אין חלק.* 
מה לכם בבנין חומת העיר הזאת כי אין לכם חלק בה:
rashi.eng: *but you have no share.* What do you have in the building of the wall of this city, for you have no share in it.

notes.51: (tn): Or “consecrated” (so NASB, NRSV); KJV, ASV “sanctified”; NCV “gave it to the Lord’s service.”
notes.52: (tc): The MT adds קִדְּשׁוּהוּ (qidshuhu, “they sanctified it”). This term is repeated from the first part of the verse, probably as an intentional scribal addition to harmonize this statement with the preceding parallel statement.
notes.53: (tc): The translation reads וְעַד (v�’ad, “and unto”) rather than the MT reading עַד (ad, “unto”). The original vav (ו) was probably dropped accidentally due to haplography with the final vav on the immediately preceding word in the MT.

rashi.heb:
*שער הצאן.* 
כך שמו של שער:
rashi.eng: *the Sheep Gate.* Such was the name of the gate.

rashi.heb:
*המה קדשוהו.* 
לאותו שער בקדושת העיר:
rashi.eng: *they hallowed it.* that gate with the sanctity of the city.

rashi.heb:
*דלתותיו.* 
של שער:
rashi.eng: *its doors.* i.e., of the gate.

rashi.heb:
*ועד מגדל המאה.* 
כך שמו של מגדל:
rashi.eng: *and until the Tower of the Hundred.* Such was the name of the tower.

notes.54: (map): For the location of Jericho see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

rashi.heb:
*ועל ידו.* 
אצל ידו בסמוך לו של כל בונה ובונה שבנו אותו בבנין של שער הצאן:
rashi.eng: *And next to it.* Next to it, near the Sheep’s Gate, each builder built.

rashi.heb:
*בנו אנשי ירחו.* 
שכך היו מנהגם הללו היו בונים כאן בחומת העיר עד תשלום בניינה המוטל עליהם והאחרים היו בונים סמוך לבנין הראשון וכך היה מנהגם בזה אחר זה עד שנבנית כל החומה:
rashi.eng: *the men of Jericho built.* Such was their custom, these would build here [their section] of the wall of the city until [the part] they were responsible for was completed, and then others would build next to the first construction. Such was their custom, one after another, until the entire wall was built.

rashi.heb:
*ועל.* 
כמו (במדבר ב׳:כ׳) ועליו מטה מנשה בסמוך וכן פתרונו סמוך לבנין ידו והמקרא לא דקדק בלשונו פעמים שהוא אומר על ידו ופעמים שהוא אומר עליו, ואחריו החזיק:
rashi.eng: *And next.* As in (Num. 2:20) “Next to him, the tribe of Manasseh” , near him, and such is its explanation, next to the construction, and Scripture was not particular in its choice of words. Sometimes it says ודי לע, and sometimes it says וילו. “And next to them he repaired.”

rashi.heb:
*ואת שער הדגים.* 
כך שם השער:
rashi.eng: *the Fish Gate.* Such was the name of the gate.

rashi.heb:
*המה קרוהו.* 
נתנו הקורות ותקרות על השער:
rashi.eng: *they laid its beams.* They placed the beams and ceilings on the gate.

rashi.heb:
*קרוהו.* 
משקל חזק כמו מן קרה דוגמת המקרה במים עליותיו (תהילים ק״ד:ג׳) וקו"ף של קרוהו אינה נהוגה לינקד בחיר"ק בענין זה מפני רי"ש של אחריה כמו ברך (שם י') חרף עשהו (משלי י״ז:ה׳) וברכתיה והיתה לגוים (ראשית י"ז) וזריתים בארצות (יחזקאל כ"ט):
rashi.eng: *they laid its beams.* Heb. קֵרוּהוּ the intensive conjugation, like “… behold he laid the beams (קֵרָה),” [which appears nowhere in Scripture;] similar to (Ps. 104:3): “Who roofs (הַמְקָרֶה) His upper chambers with water.” The “kuf” of קֵרוּהוּ is not customarily vowelized with a “hirik” in this context because of the “resh” following it, like (ibid. 10:3): “blessed (בֵּרֵךְ);” (Prov. 17:5): “blasphemed (חֵרֵף);” (Gen. 17:16): “I shall bless her (וּבֵרַכְתִּיהָ);”(Ezek. 29:12): “and I shall scatter them (וּזְרֵתִים) in the lands.”

rashi.heb:
*מנעוליו.* 
מסגריו ששוירל"ץ בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *its locks.* מַנְעוּלָיו, ses verrous in French, its bolts (locks).

rashi.heb:
*החזיק.* 
לבנות הבנין:
rashi.eng: *repaired.* Heb. הֶחֱזִיק, [lit. strengthened,] to build the building.

notes.58: (tn): The plural form אֲדֹנֵיהֶם (’adonehem, “lords”) is probably a plural of majesty referring to Nehemiah (e.g., Isa 19:4; see GKC 399 �124.i). However, some English versions take the plural to refer to the “supervisors” (NIV, NCV, TEV) and others to “their Lord” (KJV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*התקועים.* 
כך היו נקראים על שם מקומם שהיה תקוע:
rashi.eng: *the Tekoites.* They were called this because of their place, which was Tekoa.

rashi.heb:
*אדיריהם.* 
עשירים של תקוע:
rashi.eng: *but their mighty men.* the wealthy men of Tekoa.

rashi.heb:
*לא הביאו צורם.* 
לא סייעו בעבודתו של הקב"ה לבנות חומת העיר:
rashi.eng: *did not bring their neck.* They did not assist in the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, to build the wall of the city.

notes.59: (tn): Or “the Old Gate” (cf. KJV, ASV, NASB, NCV, NRSV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*ואת שער הישנה.* 
כך שמה:
rashi.eng: *And… the gate of the old [city].* Heb. הַיְשָּׁנָה, the Gate Yeshana, such was its name.

rashi.heb:
*לכסא פחת עבר הנהר.* 
כסא אחד בנה כדי לישב בו אותו פחת של עבר הנהר:
rashi.eng: *a throne for the governor of the land beyond the river.* The [people of] the land beyond the river built a throne for the governor of the land beyond the river to sit upon.

notes.61: (tc): Assuming that the MT reading וַיַּעַזְבוּ (vayya’azvu) is related to the root עָזַב I (“to abandon”) – which makes little sense contextually – some interpreters emend the MT to וַיַּעַזְרוּ (vayya’azru, “they aided”), as suggested by the editors of BHS. However, it is better to relate this term to the root II עָזַב meaning “to restore; to repair” (BDB 738 s.v. II עָזַב) or “to plaster” (HALOT 807 s.v. II עזב qal.1). This homonymic root is rare, appearing elsewhere only in Exod 23:5 and Job 9:27, where it means “to restore; to put in order” (HALOT 807-8 s.v. II עזב qal.2). The related Mishnaic Hebrew noun מעזיבה refers to a “plastered floor.” This Hebrew root is probably related to the cognate Ugaritic, Old South Arabic and Sabean verbs that mean “to restore” and “to prepare; to lay” (see BDB 738 s.v.; HALOT 807 s.v.). Some scholars in the nineteenth century suggested that this term be nuanced “paved.” However, most modern English versions have “restored” (so NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV) or “rebuilt” (so NCV, CEV).
notes.62: (tn, Heb): “[the city wall of] Jerusalem.” The term “Jerusalem” probably functions as a metonymy of association for the city wall of Jerusalem. Accordingly, the phrase “the city wall of” has been supplied in the translation to clarify this figurative expression. For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*צורפים.* 
אותה משפחה היתה נקראת על שם אומנותם:
rashi.eng: *goldsmiths.* That family was called by their craft.

rashi.heb:
*ויעזבו ירושלים.* 
מלאוה עפר עד החומה הרחבה כדי להחזיקה:
rashi.eng: *and they filled Jerusalem.* Heb. וַיַעַזְבוּ יְרוּשָּׁלַיִם They filled it with earth up to the wide wall in order to strengthen it.

rashi.heb:
*שר חצי פלך ירושלים.* 
שר היה על חצי העם שבירושלים, פלך ל' דוכסות ומלכות:
rashi.eng: *the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem.* He was the prince over half the people in Jerusalem. פֶּלֶךְ is an expression of a duchy or a kingdom.

notes.63: (tc): The translation reads נֶגֶד (neged, “before”) with a few medieval Hebrew MSS, some MSS of the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and the Vulgate, rather than וְנֶגֶד (v�neged, “and before”) of the MT.

rashi.heb:
*ונגד ביתו.* 
נפל חלקו לבנות שהיה ביתו סמוך לאותו מקום של חומת העיר:
rashi.eng: *and opposite his house.* his lot fell to build, for his house was near that place of the wall of the city.

rashi.heb:
*מדה שנית.* 
כאותה מדה אשר בנה חבירו של מעלה גם הוא בנה כמותו:
rashi.eng: *a second measure.* Just like the measurement which his friend built before [him], so he also built like [his friend.]

rashi.heb:
*מדה שנית.* 
בבנין החומה. אינו נופל לומר ל' מדה בבנין השערים לפי שאין להם כי אם בבנין חלק של חומה שלא מצינו בכל הפרשה בבנין השערים ל' מדה:
rashi.eng: *a second measure.* in the building of the wall. The expression of measure is inappropriate for the building of the gates because they have [a measure] only in the building of a part of the wall, for we do not find in the entire chapter of the building of the gates the expression of a measure.

rashi.heb:
*ואת מגדל התנורים.* 
גם הוא בנה אותו מגדל ששמו כך כל המגדלים הללו שבפרשה היו בנוים בחומת העיר סביב:
rashi.eng: *the Tower of the Furnaces.* He also built a tower by that name. All these towers in the chapter were built in the wall around the city.

notes.64: (tc): The reference to daughters, while not impossible, is odd in light of the cultural improbability that young women would participate in the strenuous labor of rebuilding city walls. All other such references in the Book of Nehemiah presuppose male laborers. Not surprisingly, some scholars suspect a textual problem. One medieval Hebrew MS and the Syriac Peshitta read וּבָנָיו (uvanayv, “and his sons”) rather than the MT reading וּבְנוֹתָיו (uv�notayv, “and his daughters”). Some scholars emend the MT to וּבֹנָיו (uvonayv, “and his builders”). On the other hand, the MT is clearly the more difficult reading, and so it is preferred.

rashi.heb:
*הוא ובנותיו.* 
שלום ובנותיו החזיקו לבנות הבנין:
rashi.eng: *he and his daughters.* Shallum and his daughters repaired the building of the structure.

notes.65: (tn, Heb): “one thousand cubits.” The standard cubit in the OT is assumed by most authorities to be about eighteen inches (45 cm) long, so this section of the wall would be about fifteen hundred feet (450 m).

rashi.heb:
*עד שער השפות.* 
ושער האשפות לא היה בכלל:
rashi.eng: *until the Dung Gate.* but the Dung Gate was not included.

notes.66: (tn): The Hebrew word translated “Siloam” is הַשֶּׁלַח (hashelakh, “water-channel”; cf. ASV, NASB, NRSV, TEV, CEV “Shelah”). It apparently refers to the Pool of Siloam whose water supply came from the Gihon Spring via Hezekiah’s Tunnel built in 701 B.C. (cf. Isa 8:6). See BDB 1019 s.v. שִׁלֹחַ; W. L. Holladay, Concise Hebrew and Aramaic Lexicon, 372. On the etymology of the word, which is a disputed matter, see HALOT 1517 s.v. III שֶׁלַח.

rashi.heb:
*שר פלך המצפה.* 
שר ודוכוס המצפה:
rashi.eng: *the ruler of the district of Mizpah.* the prince and duke of Mizpah.

rashi.heb:
*הוא יבננו.* 
הוא היה בונה אותו שער:
rashi.eng: *he built it.* he was building the same gate.

rashi.heb:
*ויטללנו.* 
והוא היה מסכך אותו לשון מטללתא:
rashi.eng: *and roofed it.* And he laid the roof on it, an expression of a ceiling (מְטַלַלְתָּא).
*and the wall of the pool of Shelah.* which inclines towards the king’s garden.
*and until the steps.* They recognized these places.

rashi.heb:
*בית צור.* 
שם מקום:
rashi.eng: *Beth Zur.* the name of a place.

notes.67: (tc): The translation reads וְעַל (v�’al, “and unto”) with several medieval Hebrew MSS and some MSS of LXX, rather than the MT reading עַל (’al, “unto”).

rashi.heb:
*לפלכו.* 
מאותה שררה חצי פלך בנה בנין זה לפלכו כ"ף דגושה כאשר יאמר מן מלך מלכו מן עבד עבדו כן יאמר מן פלך פלכו שאות אחרונה של שם דבר מאותיות בג"ד כפ"ת דגושו':
rashi.eng: *half the district.* From that bailiwick, the half district, he built this structure. In the word לְפִּלְכּוֹ, the “kaff” has a “dagesh,” as one says from מֶלֶךְ, מַלְכּוֹ, from עֶבֶד, עַבְדוֹ, so does one say from פֶּלֶךְ, פִּלְכּוֹ, for [if] the last letter of the noun is one of the letters “beth”, “gimmel”, “daleth”, “kaff”, “pey,” or “tav,” it is punctuated with a “dagesh.”

notes.69: (tc): The translation reads with a few medieval Hebrew MSS and the Syriac Peshitta בִּנֻּי (binnuy) rather than the MT reading בַּוַּי (bavvay).

rashi.heb:
*אחיהם.* 
הלוים:
rashi.eng: *their brothers.* the Levites.

rashi.heb:
*מנגד עלות הנשק.* 
כנגד אותו מקום שהיו עולים הגבורים אל הנשק לפי פשוטו של מקרא נראה שהיה שם מקום אחד בסמוך לחומה וכלי זיין של נשק הגבורים היו נותנין (ס"א נתונים) שם כענין שנאמר ערי מבצר והנשק:
rashi.eng: *opposite the ascent to the armory.* opposite the place where the mighty men would ascend to the weapons. According to the simple interpretation of the verse, it appears that there was a place near the wall where the mighty men kept their weapons, as it is stated: (II Kings 10:2) “… and cities (sic) of fortification and arms.”

rashi.heb:
*המקצוע.* 
לקרן זוית של חומה:
rashi.eng: *at the corner.* at the corner of the wall.

rashi.heb:
*החרה.* 
פתרונו לפי ענינו וכפל לשון הוא על החזוק:
rashi.eng: *repaired.* Heb. הֶחֱרָה. Its interpretation is according to the context, and it is a double expression for repairing.

notes.70: (tn, Heb): “the house of Eliashib.” This has not been repeated in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*מפתח בית אלישיב ועד תכלית וגו'.* 
מנגד אותו בית בנה בניינו:
rashi.eng: *from the entrance of the house of Eliashib until the end of, etc..* Opposite that house he built his structure.

rashi.heb:
*נגד ביתם.* 
שהיה שם בסמוך לחומה:
rashi.eng: *opposite their house.* which was there near the wall.

notes.71: (tc): The MT lacks the phrase אַחֲרָיו הֶחֱזִיק (’akharayv hekheziq, “after him worked”). This phrase is used repeatedly in Neh 3:16-31 to introduce each worker and his location. It probably dropped out accidentally through haplography.

rashi.heb:
*והמגדל היוצא.* 
מגדל אחד היה בחומה שהוא יוצא ובולט מבפנים:
rashi.eng: *and the tower that juts out.* There was one tower in the wall that jutted out and protruded from within.

notes.73: (tc): The Hebrew text lacks the verb “worked.” It is implied, however, and has been supplied in the translation.

rashi.heb:
*והנתינים היו יושבים בעופל.* 
והנתינים היו יושבים באותו מחוז והיו בונים אותו מחוז שלהם שהיה סמוך לחומה עד נגד שער המים של צד המזרח:
rashi.eng: *And the Nethinites dwelt in the Ophel.* And the Nethinites were dwelling in that district, and they were building their district, which was near the wall, until opposite the Water Gate of the eastern side.

rashi.heb:
*איש לנגד ביתו.* 
כל אחד היה בונה כנגד ביתו:
rashi.eng: *each one opposite his house.* Each one was building opposite his house.

notes.74: (tc): The translation reads אַחֲרָיו (’akharayv, “after him”) with the Qere and many medieval Hebrew MSS, rather than the reading אַחֲרֵי (’akharey, “after me”) of the MT. So also in v. 31.

rashi.heb:
*וחנון בן צלף הששי.* 
בנים הרבה היו לו לצלף וחנון הוא הששי:
rashi.eng: *and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph.* Zalaph had many sons, and Hanun was the sixth.

rashi.heb:
*מדה שני.* 
כמו שנית:
rashi.eng: *a second measure.* Heb. מִדָה שֵּׁנִי, like שֵּׁנִית.

rashi.heb:
*נשכתו.* 
כמו לשכתו לשכה אחת היתה לו שם סמוך לחומה:
rashi.eng: *his chamber.* Heb. נִשְּׁכָּתוֹ, like לִשְּׁכָּתוֹ. He had one chamber adjoining the wall.

notes.75: (tn, Heb): “Miphkad Gate” (so TEV; KJV similar); NRSV “Muster Gate.”

rashi.heb:
*בן הצורפי.* 
איש הצורף ונקרא של שם אומנותו:
rashi.eng: *the son of Hatzorefi.* the goldsmith, and he was named after his craft.

rashi.heb:
*ובין עלית הפנה לשער הצאן.* 
תחלת הבנין התחילו לבנות שער הצאן שנאמר ויבנו את שער הצאן וגו' כך היו בונין החומה מסביב בזה אחר זה:
rashi.eng: *And between the ascent to the tower and the Sheep Gate.* At the beginning of the building they began to build the Sheep Gate, as it says (verse 1): “… and they built the Sheep Gate, etc.” So did they build the wall all around, one after the other.

rashi.heb:
*לפני אחיו וחיל שומרון.* 
לפני חביריו וחיל שומרון שהיו צרי יהודה:
rashi.eng: *before his brethren and the army of Samaria.* before his brethren and the army of Samaria, who were the adversaries of Judea.

rashi.heb:
*מה היהודים.* 
מדוע היהודים כך הם עושים:
rashi.eng: *What are the Jews.* Why are the Jews doing this?

rashi.heb:
*האמללים.* 
ענין חלשות ורפיון:
rashi.eng: *the feeble.* Heb. הָאֲמֵלָלִים, a term denoting weakness and feebleness.

rashi.heb:
*היעזבו להם.* 
וכי הם סבורים אשר יעזבו ויניחו להם העובדי כוכבים לבנות:
rashi.eng: *Will they let them.* Do they think that the heathens will allow them to build?

rashi.heb:
*היזבחו.* 
אם יזבחו להם את זבחיהם תמיד כמו שהם סבורים:
rashi.eng: *Will they sacrifice.* Will they constantly slaughter their sacrifices for themselves as they think?

rashi.heb:
*היכלו ביום.* 
אם יכלו וישלימו מלאכתם אשר התחילו ביום א' לומר שלא יניחום העובדי כוכבים לגמור את בניינם:
rashi.eng: *Will they finish in one day.* Will they complete the work that they started in one day? That is to say that the heathens will not permit them to complete their building.

rashi.heb:
*היחיו.* 
אם יחיו ויתקנו ויחזירו האבנים לקדמתן להיות קשות וחזקות מן העפר:
rashi.eng: *Will they revive.* Will they revive and repair and restore stones to their previous state to be harder and stronger than the dust?

rashi.heb:
*מערמות.* 
ענין חמרים ותלים:
rashi.eng: *from the heaps.* Heb. מֵעֲרֵמוֹת, a term denoting heaps and mounds.

*for they are burnt.* The stones were burnt and have become dust. So did they jeer and ridicule the building of the wall, which they were building from the burnt stones that had fallen to the earth from the fire when Jerusalem was burned.

rashi.heb:
*וטוביה העמוני אצלו.* 
טוביה היה אצלו של סנבלט:
rashi.eng: *And Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him.* Tobiah was beside Sanballat.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמר.* 
וכך היה אומר ומלעיג:
rashi.eng: *and he said.* And so he was saying and ridiculing.

rashi.heb:
*גם אשר הם בונים.* 
אף הבנין הזה אשר הם בונים:
rashi.eng: *Even what they build.* even this building that they are building.

rashi.heb:
*אם יעלה שועל.* 
על הבנין לפרוץ חומת העיר מה יהא עליו לומר שאין לבנין תקנה וכל מי שירצה יבא ויפרוץ בו:
rashi.eng: *if a fox comes up.* on the building to breach the wall of the city, what will become of it? That is to say that the building cannot be repaired, and whoever wishes, can come and break into it.

rashi.heb:
*שמע אלהינו.* 
כאשר שמעתי בלעגם עלינו התפללתי תפילה זאת:
rashi.eng: *Hearken, our God.* When I heard their ridicule of us, I prayed this prayer.

rashi.heb:
*בארץ שביה.* 
שיגלו מעל אדמתם כאשר גלינו:
rashi.eng: *in a land of captivity.* that they be exiled from the land as we were exiled.

rashi.heb:
*ואל תכס.* 
כמו ואל תכסה דוגמת וסוד אחר אל תגל (משלי כ"א) כמו אל תגלה:
rashi.eng: *And do not conceal.* Heb. תְּכַס וְאַל, like וְאַל תְּכַסֶה, similar to (Prov. 25:9): “… but do not divulge (תְּגָל) another’s secret,” like תְּגַלֶה.

rashi.heb:
*כי הכעיסו.* 
אשר הכעיסו נגד הבונים להלעיגם:
rashi.eng: *for they have provoked.* that they have provoked the builders to ridicule them.

rashi.heb:
*ותקשר.* 
כאשר נתקשרה החומה ונבנית עד חציה אז היה לב העם להוט ומשוך לעשות בנין החומה:
rashi.eng: *was built.* Heb. וַתִּקָשֵּׁר, lit. it was bound. When the wall was bound up and built to its half, the people were eager and anxious to complete their building of it.

notes.76: (sn): Beginning with , the verse numbers through in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with ET = HT, ET = HT, ET = HT, ET = HT, ET = HT, ET = HT, ET = HT, etc., through ET = HT. Thus in the Hebrew Bible chap. 3 of the Book of Nehemiah has 38 verses, while chap. 4 has only 17 verses.

rashi.heb:
*כי עלתה ארוכה.* 
שנבנתה החומה:
rashi.eng: *was repaired.* Heb. עָלְתָה אָרוּכָה, [lit. attained a cure,] that the wall was built.

rashi.heb:
*ארוכה.* 
ענין חובש ותרופה:
rashi.eng: *repaired.* A [word having the] meaning of bandaging and healing.

rashi.heb:
*כי החלו הפרוצים להסתם.* 
אשר התחילו אנשי העיר שהיו פרוצים עד עתה מאין חומה היו עתה סתומים בבנין החומה:
rashi.eng: *that the people who were exposed had commenced to be closed in.* that the people of the city, who had heretofore been exposed without a wall, were now closed in by the building of the wall.

notes.78: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
notes.79: (tc): The Hebrew text is difficult here. The present translation follows the MT, but the text may be corrupt. H. G. M. Williamson (Ezra, Nehemiah [WBC], 213-14) translates these words as “Will they commit their cause to God?” suggesting that MT לָהֶם (lahem, “to them”) should be emended to לֵאלֹהִים (lelohim, “to God”), a proposal also found in the apparatus of BHS. In his view later scribes altered the phrase out of theological motivations. J. Blenkinsopp’s translation is similar: “Are they going to leave it all to God?” (Ezra–Nehemiah [OTL], 242-44). However, a problem for this view is the absence of external evidence to support the proposed emendation. The sense of the MT reading may be the notion that the workers – if left to their own limited resources – could not possibly see such a demanding and expensive project through to completion. This interpretation understands the collocation עָזַב (’azav, “to leave”) plus לְ (l�, “to”) to mean “commit a matter to someone,” with the sense in this verse “Will they leave the building of the fortified walls to themselves?”

rashi.heb:
*ולעשות לו תועה.* 
לעשות לו בבנין החומה קלקול והשחתה תועה כמו ולדבר אל ה' תועה (ישעיהו ל״ב:ו׳):
rashi.eng: *and to wreak destruction therein.* to wreak upon the building of the wall ruin and destruction. It is like (Isa. 32:5): “… and to speak destructively (תּוֹעָה) about the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*עליהם.* 
על הבונים:
rashi.eng: *over them.* over the builders.

rashi.heb:
*מפניהם.* 
מפני האויבים:
rashi.eng: *because of them.* because of the enemies.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמר יהודה.* 
כך היו אומרים ומתאוננים אנשי יהודה:
rashi.eng: *And Judea said.* So were the people of Judea saying and complaining.

rashi.heb:
*כשל כח הסבל.* 
הסובלים ועומסים האבנים והעצים לבנין החומה נכשלו בכחם שאין בהם כח לבנות מפני האויבים:
rashi.eng: *The porter’s strength has failed.* Those who bear and load the stones and the wood for the building of the wall have failed in their strength, for they have no more strength to build because of the enemies.

rashi.heb:
*ועפר הרבה.* 
עדיין יש טיט וחומר הרבה ליתן בבנין החומה לומר שעדיין המלאכה גדולה עלינו לבנות ואנחנו לא נוכל לבנות בחומה מפני פחד האויבים:
rashi.eng: *and there is much earth.* There is still much mud and clay to place into the wall, meaning that we still have much work, but we cannot build because of fear of the enemies.

notes.80: (tn): The Hiphil stem of כָּעַס (ka’as) may mean: (1) “to provoke to anger”; (2) “to bitterly offend”; or (3) “to grieve” (BDB 495 s.v. Hiph.; HALOT 491 s.v. כעס hif). The Hebrew lexicons suggest that “bitterly offend” is the most appropriate nuance here.
notes.81: (tn, Heb): “before the builders.” The preposition נֶגֶד (neged, “before”) here connotes “in the sight of” or “in the view of” (BDB 617 s.v. 1.a; HALOT 666 s.v. 1.a).

rashi.heb:
*ויאמרו צרינו.* 
כך היה נחמיה מספר והולך:
rashi.eng: *And our adversaries said.* Nehemiah proceeds to tell this.

rashi.heb:
*לא ידעו ולא יראו.* 
כך היו אומרים צרינו עלינו לא ידעו ולא יכירו ישראל בנו עד אשר נבוא פתאום לתוכם ונהרוג אותם ובדבר זה נשבות ונבטל הבנין:
rashi.eng: *They will not know, and they will not see.* So were our adversaries saying about us: “They will not know, and the Israelites will not recognize us until we come suddenly into their midst and kill them, and with this plot we will stop and curtail the building.”

notes.83: (tn, Heb): “the people had a heart to work.”

rashi.heb:
*ויהי כאשר באו היהודים.* 
ועתה נאספו הצרים אשר נתקשרו יחד לבא להלחם בנו עם היהודים אשר היו בינותם בארצותם ואותם היהודים אשר נתחברו עמהם באו לפני החיל כדרך אנשי המלחמה לדבר אלינו ובענין הזה הערימו היהודים את האויבים ויהי כאשר באו היהודים היושבים אצלם וגו':
rashi.eng: *Now it came to pass when the Jews came.* And now, the adversaries who had conspired together to wage war against us gathered with the Jews who were among them in their lands, and those Jews who had joined them came before the army, as is customary for soldiers to do, to speak to us, and in this manner the Jews conspired against the enemies. Now it came to pass when the Jews who dwelt beside them came, etc.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמרו לנו עשר פעמים.* 
התרו בנו אותם היהודים עד עשר פעמים להלחם באויבינו כי הם באים למלחמה וכך אמרו לנו מכל המקומות וגו' מכל אותן המקומות שתהיו נפוצים שם בבנין החומה אנה ואנה תהיו זהירים להיות נאספים יחד עד אשר תשובו עלינו ביחד להלחם בנו:
rashi.eng: *that they said to us ten times.* Those Jews warned us as many as ten times to wage war against our enemies because they were coming to war. And this is what they said to us, “From all the places, etc.” From all those places where you will be scattered while building the wall, here and there, be careful to assemble until you return upon us together to wage war against us.

notes.84: (sn): Chapter 4 begins here in the Hebrew text (BHS). See the note at 4:1.
notes.85: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*ואעמיד מתחתיות.* 
לחומה, כאשר שמעתי דבריהם העמדתי מתחתיות לאותו מקום סביב לירושלים מאחורי לחומת העיר:
rashi.eng: *So I stationed from below… the wall.* When I heard their words, I stationed [mighty men] from below that place around Jerusalem, from behind the wall of the city and on the bare rocks.

rashi.heb:
*בצחיחים.* 
למשפחות מן העם מגבורים שבהם עם כלי זיין שבהם להלחם באויבינו כאשר יבאו:
rashi.eng: *according to families.* of the people, of the mighty men among them with their weapons, to fight against our enemies when they would come.

rashi.heb:
*ואעמיד מתחתיות וגו'.* 
ואעמיד את העם וגו' מקרא זה דוגמת והיו המים אשר תקח מן היאור וגו' והיו לדם ביבשת (שמות ד׳:ט׳) כי הנה אויביך ה' כי הנה אויביך יאבדו (תהילים צ״ב:י׳) עורי עורי דבורה עורי עורי דברי שיר (שופטים ה׳:י״ב) לא לנו ה' לא לנו (תהילים קט״ו:א׳):
rashi.eng: *And I stationed from below, etc. and I stationed the people, etc..* This verse follows the pattern of (Exod. 4:9): “… and the water that you will take from the river will be… will become blood on the dry land;” (Ps. 92:10): “For behold, Your enemies, O Lord, for behold, Your enemies shall perish;” (Jud. 5:12): “Praise! Praise! Deborah. Praise! Praise! Utter a song;” (Ps. 115:1): “Not to us, O Lord, not to us.”

rashi.heb:
*וארא ואקום.* 
וכאשר ראיתי האויבים באים קמתי לדבר אל החורים והסגנים לזרזם להלחם באויבינו:
rashi.eng: *And I saw, and I arose.* And when I saw the enemies coming, I arose to speak to the nobles and to the prefects to spur them to fight against our enemy.

rashi.heb:
*על אחיכם.* 
בשביל אחיכם:
rashi.eng: *for your brethren.* Heb. עַל אֲחֵיכֶם, for the sake of your brethren.

notes.87: (tn, Heb): “against them.” The words “to protect” are added in the translation for the sake of clarity and smoothness. Some emend MT עֲלֵיהֶם (’alehem, “against them”) to עָלֶיהָ (’aleha, “against it,” i.e., Jerusalem).

rashi.heb:
*כי נודע לנו.* 
הדבר אשר באו להלחם בנו:
rashi.eng: *that it had become known to us.* that they were coming to fight against us.

rashi.heb:
*ונשב כלנו.* 
חזרנו כלנו ממקום שנאספנו יחד לקראת האויבים כל אחד ואחד במלאכתו לבנין החומה:
rashi.eng: *and we all returned.* We all returned from the place where we had gathered to meet the enemies, each one to his work in the building of the wall.

rashi.heb:
*ויהי מן היום ההוא.* 
ומאותו יום והלאה היו חצי הגבורים עושים בבנין החומה ושאר חצי הגבורים היו מזויינים בכלי זיינם לשמור אחיהם העושים במלאכה:
rashi.eng: *And it was from that day on.* And from that day on, half the mighty men worked at the building of the wall, and the remaining half of the mighty men were armed with weapons to guard their brethren who were doing the work.

rashi.heb:
*והרמחים.* 
וי"ו יתירה כמו וי"ו של ואיה וענה (ראשית לו):
rashi.eng: *spears.* Heb. וְהָרְמָחִים. The “vav” is superfluous, like the “vav” of (Gen. 36:24): “And these are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah (וְאַיָה) and Anah.”

rashi.heb:
*והשרים.* 
היו מחוברים אחרי כל שבט יהודה להיות זהירים במלחמה:
rashi.eng: *and the rulers.* were close behind the entire tribe of Judah to be cautious in the battle.

rashi.heb:
*הבונים בחומה וגו'.* 
אותם שהיו בונין ואותן שהיו עומסים ונושאים המשאות ביד אחת היו עושים מלאכתן וביד אחת היו נושאים כלי זיין:
rashi.eng: *The builders of the wall, etc..* Those who were building the wall and those who were loading and carrying the loads were working with one hand, and carrying weapons with the other.

rashi.heb:
*השלח.* 
כלי קרב כמו מעבור בשלח (איוב ל״ג:י״ח) וכן חברו מנחם:
rashi.eng: *the sword.* Heb. הַשָּׁלַח, an implement of war, like (Job 33:18): "… from perishing by the sword (מֵעֲבֹר בַּשָּׁלַח). And so did Menahem associate it (Machbereth Menahem p. 174).

notes.92: (tc): The MT reads the anomalous מִכָּל־הַמְּקֹמוֹת (mikkol hamm�qomot, “from every place”) but the BHS editors propose כָּל־הַמְּזִמּוֹת (kol hamm�zimmot, “about every scheme”). The initial mem (מ) found in the MT may have been added accidentally due to dittography with the final mem (ם) on the immediately preceding word, and the MT qof (ק) may have arisen due to orthographic confusion with the similar looking zayin (ז). The emendation restores sense to the line in the MT, which makes little sense and features an abrupt change of referents: “Wherever you turn, they will be upon us!” The threat was not against the villagers living nearby but against those repairing the wall, as the following context indicates. See also the following note on the word “plotting.”
notes.93: (tc): The MT reads תָּשׁוּבוּ (tashuvu, “you turn”) which is awkward contextually. The BHS editors propose emending to חָשְׁבוּ (hash�vu, “they were plotting”) which harmonizes well with the context. This emendation involves mere orthographic confusion between similar looking ח (khet) and ת (tav), and the resultant dittography of middle vav (ו) in MT. See also the preceding note on the word “schemes.”

rashi.heb:
*והבונים.* 
כיצד הם בונים שהיו כולם חגורים איש חרבו על מתניו ובונים:
rashi.eng: *And the builders.* How were they building? They were all girded, each one with his sword on his waist, and thus did they build.

rashi.heb:
*אצלי.* 
הוא היה תדיר אצלי:
rashi.eng: *beside me.* He was always beside me.

notes.94: (tc): The MT preserves the anomalous Kethib form צְחִחִיִּים (ts�khikhiyyim); the Qere reads צְחִיחִים (ts�khikhim) which is preferred (BDB 850 s.v. צָהִיחַ; HALOT 1018 s.v. *צָהִיחַ). The meaning of the Hebrew term צְחִיחִים (ts�khikhim) here is uncertain. Elsewhere (Ezek 24:7, 8; 26:4, 14) it refers to a shining or glaring surface of a rock (BDB 850 s.v. צָהִיחַ; HALOT 1018 s.v. *צָהִיחַ), but here it refers to an exposed or vulnerable portion of the wall: “open positions of the wall” (HALOT 1018 s.v. 2).

rashi.heb:
*הרבה.* 
היא גדולה:
rashi.eng: *much.* Heb. הַרְבֵּה, a great [amount of work].

notes.96: (tn): The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here is אֲדֹנָי (’adonay).

rashi.heb:
*ילחם לנו.* 
ילחם בעדינו:
rashi.eng: *will fight for us.* [as translated,] will fight for us.

notes.99: (tc): The MT reads “and spears.” The conjunction should be deleted.

rashi.heb:
*איש ונערו.* 
כל אחד ואחד מן הבונים ובחור אחד עמו:
rashi.eng: *Let each man and his youth.* each of the builders and a youth with him.

rashi.heb:
*ילינו בתוך ירושלים.* 
והלילה היה להם למשמר והיום עושים מלאכה נמצא שלא היו ישנים כלום:
rashi.eng: *lodge in the midst of Jerusalem.* And the night was for their watch, and [during] the day they were doing work. The result was that they did not sleep at all.

notes.101: (tn): The first words of v. 17, “who were rebuilding the wall,” should be taken with the latter part of v. 16.
notes.102: (tn, Heb): “were carrying loads.” The LXX reads ἐν ὅπλοις (en hoplois, “with weapons”).

rashi.heb:
*אין אנחנו פושטים בגדינו.* 
תמיד היינו זריזים במשמר:
rashi.eng: *we did not take off our clothes.* We were always zealous in guarding.

rashi.heb:
*איש שלחו המים.* 
מיסב על אין שלמעלה כמו (שמואל א' ב') יצא עתק מפיכם אין איש ממנו פושט בגדיו לשכב או לרחוץ אותם במים וכפל לשון הוא על אין אנחנו פושטים:
rashi.eng: *man took it even to the water.* This refers back to “not” above, like (I Sam. 2:3): “… let not arrogance come out of your mouth.” None of us would take off his clothes to lie down or to wash them with water, and this is a double expression, [repeating,] we did not undress.

rashi.heb:
*שלחו.* 
הפשט כמו (ויקרא ו׳:ד׳) ופשט את בגדיו דמתורגם ושלח:
rashi.eng: *took it off.* Heb. שִּׁלְחוֹ, taking off, like (Lev. 6:4): “He shall then take off his garments,” which is translated by Targum as וְיִשְּׁלַח.

notes.105: (tn, Heb): “and we were doing the work.”
notes.107: (tn, Heb): “from the coming up of the dawn till the coming forth of the stars.”

notes.110: (tc, Heb): “a man, his weapon, the waters.” The MT, if in fact it is correct, is elliptical and difficult. Some scholars emend the MT reading הַמָּיִם (hammayim, “the waters”) to בִּמִנוֹ (bimino, “in his right hand”; cf. NAB, NRSV) or מִינוּ(י)הֵ (heminu, “they held on the right side”).

rashi.heb:
*ותהי צעקת העם ונשיהם גדולה.* 
דלת העם העניים היו צועקים מאד:
rashi.eng: *Now the cry of the people and their wives was great.* The poor people were crying exceedingly.

rashi.heb:
*אל אחיהם היהודים.* 
בשביל אחיהם היהודים העשירים:
rashi.eng: *about their brothers, the Jews.* about their brothers, the rich Jews.

rashi.heb:
*ויש אשר אומרים.* 
נותן טעם לדבריו למה היו צועקים יש מהם מדלת העם שהיו אומרים אנחנו רבים עם בנינו ובנותינו ונקחה דגן ועתה יש לנו למכור בנינו ובנותינו ליקח מהם דגן למען נחיה כך היו צועקים על היהודים העשירים שלא היו רוצים לפרנסם:
rashi.eng: *There were some who were saying.* He gives a reason for his words: Why were they crying? Some of the poor people were saying, “We are many with our sons and daughters and have to buy corn. Now we will have to sell our sons and daughters in order to buy corn in order to live.” So were they crying about the rich Jews who did not wish to support them.

rashi.heb:
*ויש אשר אומרים שדותינו וגו'.* 
ויש מהם בעניים שהיו מתאוננים ואומרים שדות וכרמים ובתים נתן לאחרים בערבון ומשכון ליקח דגן למזונותינו:
rashi.eng: *And there were some who were saying “Our fields, etc.”.* And there were some among the poor who were complaining and saying “Our fields, vineyards and houses we shall give to others as a pledge and as security to buy corn for our food.”

rashi.heb:
*ברעב.* 
אחרי שאין מוותרים לנו העשירים מנכסיהם לפרנסתינו:
rashi.eng: *for the hunger.* since the rich do not give any of their property up to us for our support.

notes.113: (tn, Heb): “for the tax of the king.”

rashi.heb:
*ויש אשר אומרים לוינו כסף.* 
ויש מהם אשר אומרים כבר לוינו כסף מאחרים על שדותינו וכרמינו לפרוע מס המלך ומעכשיו אין לנו כלום לצורך פרנסתינו:
rashi.eng: *And there were some who were saying, “We have borrowed money”.* And there were some who were saying, “We have already borrowed money from others on our fields and our vineyards to pay the king’s tax, and now we have nothing for our support.”

rashi.heb:
*למדת המלך.* 
למס המלך כמו (עזרא ד') מנדה בלו והלך:
rashi.eng: *for the king’s tax.* Heb. לְמִדַּת, for the king’s tax, like (Ezra 4:13): “… the king’s due (מִנְדָּה), the head tax, and the meal tax.”

notes.114: (tn, Heb): “according to the flesh of our brothers is our flesh.”
notes.116: (tn, Heb): “to become slaves” (also later in this verse).
notes.117: (tn, Heb): “there is not power for our hand.” The Hebrew expression used here is rather difficult.
notes.118: (sn): The poor among the returned exiles were being exploited by their rich countrymen. Moneylenders were loaning large amounts of money, and not only collecting interest on loans which was illegal (Lev 25:36-37; Deut 23:19-20), but also seizing pledges as collateral (Neh 5:3) which was allowed (Deut 24:10). When the debtors missed a payment, the moneylenders would seize their collateral: their fields, vineyards and homes. With no other means of income, the debtors were forced to sell their children into slavery, a common practice at this time (Neh 5:5). Nehemiah himself was one of the moneylenders (Neh 5:10), but he insisted that seizure of collateral from fellow Jewish countrymen was ethically wrong (Neh 5:9).

rashi.heb:
*ועתה כבשר אחינו בשרינו.* 
ועכשיו אנו חשובים ומיוחסים כאחינו שהם עשירים:
rashi.eng: *And now, like the flesh of our brethren is our flesh.* And now, we are as esteemed and distinguished as our brethren who are rich.

rashi.heb:
*כבניהם בנינו.* 
כבניהם שהם חשובים ומיוחסים כמו כן מיוחסים בנינו:
rashi.eng: *like their children are our children.* Like their children, who are esteemed and distinguished, so are our children distinguished.

rashi.heb:
*והנה אנחנו כובשים.* 
ועתה יש לנו להיות כובשים ונותנים בנינו ובנותינו לאחרים על עסק מזונותינו:
rashi.eng: *and behold, we are subjecting.* And now we have to subject and deliver our sons and daughters to others for the sake of our sustenance.

rashi.heb:
*ויש מבנותינו נכבשות.* 
וכבר יש קצת מבנותינו שהן נכבשות לאחרים לעבדות:
rashi.eng: *and some of our daughters are subjected.* And already there are some of our daughters who are subjected to others in slavery.

rashi.heb:
*ואין לאל ידינו.* 
ואין כח בידינו לפדותם:
rashi.eng: *and we have no power.* We do not have the ability to redeem them.

rashi.heb:
*ושדותינו וכרמינו לאחרים.* 
אף שדות וכרמים מסרנו ביד אחרים לפרנסתינו ומה נאכל מעתה כי אין לנו במה להתפרנס:
rashi.eng: *and others have our fields and vineyards.* We have even delivered our fields and vineyards to others for our sustenance. From now on, what shall we eat? We have nothing with which to sustain ourselves.

notes.120: (tn, Heb): “my heart was advised upon me.”
notes.122: (tn, Heb): “taking a creditor’s debt.” The Hebrew noun מַשָּׁא (masha’) means “interest; debt” and probably refers to the collateral (pledge) collected by a creditor (HALOT 641-42 s.v.). This particular noun form appears only in Nehemiah (5:7, 10; 10:32); however, it is related to מַשָּׁאָה (masha’ah, “contractual loan; debt; collateral”) which appears elsewhere (Deut 24:10; Prov 22:26; cf. Neh 5:11). See the note on the word “people” at the end of v. 5. The BHS editors suggest emending the MT to מָשָׂא (masa’, “burden”), following several medieval Hebrew MSS; however, the result is not entirely clear: “you are bearing a burden, a man with his brothers.”

rashi.heb:
*וימלך.* 
ויועץ לבי בעצמי:
rashi.eng: *And I thought this over to myself.* Heb. וַיִמָלֵךְ לִבִּי עָלַי, and my heart took counsel within myself.

rashi.heb:
*ואריבה.* 
נתוכחתי עם החורים והסגנים שהם העשירים:
rashi.eng: *and I contended.* I contended with the nobles and the prefects, who were the rich people.

rashi.heb:
*משא איש באחיו אתם.* 
נושים מדוע אתם כך עושים היה לכם לפרנס העניים הללו ואתם מלוים להם ממון לכבוש בניהם ובנותיהם ושדותיהם וכרמיהם ובתיהם:
rashi.eng: *“Are you demanding each other’s loans?”.* Why are you doing this? You should have supported these poor people, but you are lending them money in order to appropriate their sons and daughters, their fields, vineyards and houses.

rashi.heb:
*ואתן עליהם קהלה גדולה.* 
הקהלתי ואספתי עליהם קהילה גדולה לצעוק עליהם כדי לביישם:
rashi.eng: *and I gathered a large assembly around them.* I congregated and gathered a large assembly around them to shout at them in order to embarrass them.

rashi.heb:
*ואמרה להם.* 
וכן אמרתי להם אנחנו קנינו כבר את אחינו היהודים אשר בשביה מיד העכו"ם שהיו נמכרים להם:
rashi.eng: *And I said to them.* And so I said to them: We already bought our Jewish brethren who were in captivity from the heathens to whom they were sold.

rashi.heb:
*כדי בנו.* 
באותו די ממון שבידינו:
rashi.eng: *with as much as we could afford.* with as much money as was in our hands.

rashi.heb:
*וגם אתם.* 
ואף אתם תמכרו לעכו"ם את אחיכם הנכבשים תחת ידיכם לעבדים:
rashi.eng: *and you too.* And you too will sell to the heathens your brethren who are subjected to you as slaves?

rashi.heb:
*ונמכרו לנו.* 
והמעשה יבא לידי כך שיהיו מכורים לנו מיד העכו"ם (אם כן למה תמכרו אותם כיון שמוכרחים אנחנו לפדותם כן הוא בס"א):
rashi.eng: *and they will be sold to us.* And the result will be that they will be sold to us by the heathens (and if so, why should you sell them, since we will be compelled to redeem them? This is found in certain editions).

rashi.heb:
*ויחרישו.* 
שתקו ונתביישו ולא ידעו מה להשיב:
rashi.eng: *and they remained silent.* They were silent and ashamed, and they did not know what to answer.

notes.127: (tc): The translation reads with the Qere and the ancient versions וָאוֹמַר (va’omar, “and I said”) rather than the MT Kethib, וַיֹּאמֶר (vayyo’mer, “and he said”).
notes.128: (tn, Heb): “not good.” The statement “The thing…is not good” is an example of tapeinosis, a figurative expression which emphasizes the intended point (“The thing…is wrong!”) by negating its opposite.

rashi.heb:
*לא טוב הדבר.* 
רע הדבר בפני הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *The thing… is not good.* The thing is evil in the eyes of the Holy One, blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*מחרפת.* 
מפני חרפות העכו"ם שהם אויבינו:
rashi.eng: *because of the reproach.* because of the reproach of the heathens who are our enemies.

notes.132: (tn, Heb): “this debt.” This expression is a metonymy of association: “debt” refers to the seizure of the collateral of the debt.

rashi.heb:
*וגם אני אחי ונערי.* 
אף אני וחבירי נושים בהם ממון ואנחנו נעזוב ונמחול להם כל ההלואות הללו:
rashi.eng: *I, too, and my brothers and my servants.* I, too, and my colleagues lent them money, and we shall abandon and relinquish to them all these loans.

rashi.heb:
*נושים.* 
כמו (מלכים ב ד׳:א׳) והנושה בא לקחת:
rashi.eng: *have lent.* Heb. נֹשִׁים, like (II Kings 4:1): “… and the creditor (וְהַנֹשֶּׁה) has come to take.”

notes.133: (tc): The MT reads וּמְאַת (um�’at, “and the hundredth”) which is somewhat enigmatic. The BHS editors suggest emending to וּמַשַּׁאת (umasha’t, “and the debt”) which refers to the interest or collateral (pledge) seized by a creditor (Deut 24:10; Prov 22:26; see HALOT 641-42 s.v. מַשָּׁא). The term מַשַּׁאת (masha’t) is related to the noun מָשָּׁא (masha’, “debt”) in 5:7, 10.

rashi.heb:
*השיבו נא.* 
ואף אתם תעשו כמוני למחול להם כל חובותיהם:
rashi.eng: *give back.* And you shall also do as I do, to relinquish all their debts to them.

rashi.heb:
*ומאת הכסף.* 
ורוב הכסף שהם חייבים לכם עם הדגן ותירוש וגו':
rashi.eng: *and the hundred silver pieces.* and the large amount of money that they owe you with the corn and the wine, etc.

notes.134: (tn): The words “these things” are not included in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied in the translation for clarity.
notes.135: (tn, Heb): “took an oath from them”; the referents (the wealthy and the officials, cf. v. 7) have been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמרו נשיב.* 
והם אמרו להשיב ולמחול הכל:
rashi.eng: *And they said, “We shall return”.* And they said [that they were willing] to return and to relinquish all.

rashi.heb:
*לעשות כדבר הזה.* 
שיהו מוחלים גם הם:
rashi.eng: *to do according to this promise.* that they too should relinquish.

rashi.heb:
*גם חצני נערתי.* 
אף אני בגדי נערתי חצני כמו (ישעיהו מ״ט:כ״ב) והביאו בניך בחוצן:
rashi.eng: *I also shook out my garment.* Heb. חָצְנִי, I also shook out my garment. חָצְנִי is like (Isa. 49:22): “… and they shall bring your sons on the skirt of their garments (בְּחֹצֶן).”

rashi.heb:
*נערתי.* 
אישקוליי"ר בלע"ז כמו התנערי מעפר (שם):
rashi.eng: *my garment.* is escrol(l)e in Old French, I shook out, like (ibid. 52:2): “Shake yourself (הִתְנַעֲרִי) from the dust.”

rashi.heb:
*ככה ינער.* 
ככה ינער הקב"ה מן העולם ומנכסיהם כל אותם שלא יהיו מוחלין חובותיהם:
rashi.eng: *So shall… shake out.* So shall the Holy One, blessed be He, shake out from the world and from their property those who do not relinquish their debts.

rashi.heb:
*נעור ורק.* 
בלא נכסים:
rashi.eng: *shake out and empty.* without property.

notes.140: (tc): The BHS editors suggest reading צֻוֵּאתִי (tsuvve’ti, “and I was appointed”) rather than the reading of the MT, אֹתִי צִוָּה (tsivvah ’oti, “he appointed me”).
notes.141: (tc): The translation reads with one medieval Hebrew MS פֶּחָה (pekhah, “governor”) rather than פֶּחָם (pekham, “their governor”) of the MT. One would expect the form with pronominal suffix to have a tav (ת) before the suffix.
notes.143: (tn, Heb): “the food of the governor.” Cf. v. 18.

rashi.heb:
*אשר צוה אותי.* 
המלך:
rashi.eng: *that he commanded me.* i.e., the king.

rashi.heb:
*פחם.* 
כמו פחה שלטן דוגמת רוקם שהוא כמו רקה:
rashi.eng: *governor.* Heb. פֶּחָם, like פֶּחָה, ruler, after the pattern of רֵיקָם, empty, like רֵיקָה.

rashi.heb:
*משנת עשרים.* 
למלך דריוש כי אז עלה מבבל שנאמר (לעיל ב) ויהי בחדש ניסן שנת עשרים וגו':
rashi.eng: *from the twentieth year.* of King Darius, for then he ascended from Babylon, as it is stated (2:1): “Now it came to pass in the month of Nissan in the twentieth year, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*שנים שתים עשרה.* 
שהם שתים עשרה שנה:
rashi.eng: *twelve years.* which equal twelve years.

rashi.heb:
*אני ואחי.* 
אני וחברי אשר באו עמי:
rashi.eng: *my brethren and I.* I and my colleagues who came with me.

rashi.heb:
*לחם הפחה לא אכלתי.* 
לחם שהוא ראוי למאכל הפחה שהעם נותנין אותו אל הפחה מן המס:
rashi.eng: *have not eaten the food allotted to the governor.* the food that was fit for the governor, which the people give the governor from the tax.

notes.144: (tc): The Hebrew term אַחַר (’akhar) is difficult here. It normally means “after,” but that makes no sense here. Some scholars emend it to אַחַד (’akhad) and supply the word “day,” which yields the sense “daily.” Cf. TEV “40 silver coins a day for food and wine.”

rashi.heb:
*הכבידו על העם.* 
הכבידו מס על העם:
rashi.eng: *burdened the people.* Heb. הִכְבִּידוּ, lit. made heavy. They made the tax heavy upon the people.

rashi.heb:
*ויקחו.* 
והיו לוקחים מהם בשביל המס לחם ויין אחר נתינת ארבעים שקלים של כסף וכך היו רגילים בכל שנה:
rashi.eng: *and took.* They would take bread and wine from them for the tax after they had already given forty silver shekels, and they were accustomed to doing this every year.

rashi.heb:
*גם נעריהם.* 
של פחות:
rashi.eng: *also their servants.* [i.e., the servants] of the governors.

rashi.heb:
*החומה.* 
חומת העיר:
rashi.eng: *wall.* the wall of the city.

rashi.heb:
*החזקתי.* 
התעסקתי לעסוק בה תדיר:
rashi.eng: *I adhered.* I busied myself to engage in it constantly.

rashi.heb:
*ושדה לא קנינו.* 
ובשדות של היהודים שהיו בונים החומה לא קנינו אני ובני סייעתי על עסק דוחקם שהיו עוסקין בבנין החומה אבל הייתי נותן להם ממון כדי לבנות הבנין:
rashi.eng: *and we did not buy a field.* But neither I nor my associates bought the fields of the Jews who were building the wall because of their poverty; they were engaged in building the wall, but I gave them money in order to build the wall.

rashi.heb:
*על המלאכה.* 
לבנות תדיר:
rashi.eng: *over the work.* to build constantly.

notes.146: (tn, Heb): “who were gathered around us at my table.”
notes.147: (tn): Or “from the Gentiles.” The same Hebrew word can refer to “the Gentiles” or “the nations.” Cf. the phrase in 6:16.

rashi.heb:
*מאה וחמשים איש.* 
היו אוכלים על שולחני לבד הגרים הבאים אלינו מן העכו"ם שאף הם היו אוכלים על שלחני:
rashi.eng: *one hundred and fifty men.* were eating at my table, in addition to the proselytes who came to us from the gentiles, for they too were eating at my table.

rashi.heb:
*ואשר היה נעשה.* 
ובכל יום ויום היו אוכלים על שולחני שור אחד ושש צאן וצפרים הרבה:
rashi.eng: *And what was prepared.* And every day they ate at my table one ox, six sheep and many birds.

rashi.heb:
*ברורות.* 
פתרונו לפי עניינו שש צאן עשויות כענין שנאמר חמש צאן עשויות (שמואל א כ״ה:י״ח):
rashi.eng: *prepared.* Heb. בְּרֻרוֹת. Its interpretation is according to the context: six prepared sheep, like the matter that is stated (I Sam. 25:18): “… five prepared (עֲשׂוּיוֹת) sheep.”

rashi.heb:
*נעשו לי.* 
לשון תקון כמו ובן הבקר אשר עשה (בראשית י״ח:ח׳):
rashi.eng: *were prepared for me.* Heb. נַעֲשּׂוּ, an expression of preparation, like (Gen. 18:8): “… and the calf that he had prepared (עָשָּׂה).”

rashi.heb:
*ובין עשרת ימים.* 
ובכל יום ויום היו שותים יין הרבה כדי שיעור ספוק של עשרת ימים:
rashi.eng: *and as much as ten days’ supply.* Heb. וּבֵין עֲשֶּׂרֶת יָמִים, lit. and between ten days. And every day they drank much wine, the amount that suffices for ten days.

rashi.heb:
*ועם זה.* 
ובשביל כל מעשה זה שהייתי מוציא הוצאות כל כך:
rashi.eng: *and for this.* Heb. וְעִם זֶה; and this procedure, for which I used to make such big expenditures.

rashi.heb:
*לחם.* 
של מס הראוי לפחה לא בקשתי ולא שאלתי מן העם שהרי כבדה וחזקה עבודת בנין החומה עליהם:
rashi.eng: *food.* of the tax, which is fit for the governor, I did not seek, and I did not request it of the people, for the work of the building of the wall was heavy and strong upon them.

rashi.heb:
*ולא נותר בה.* 
בחומת העיר:
rashi.eng: *and no breach was left therein.* in the wall of the city.

rashi.heb:
*דלתות לא העמדתי.* 
שלא נעשו דלתות בשערי העיר:
rashi.eng: *I had not erected.* that doors were not made in the gates of the city.

notes.148: (tn): It is not entirely clear whether the Hebrew word כְּפִירִים (k�firim) is a place-name not mentioned elsewhere in the OT (as indicated in the present translation; so also NAB, NASB) or whether it means “in [one of] the villages” (so, e.g., NIV, NRSV, NLT; see BDB 499 s.v.; HALOT 493 s.v.). The LXX and Vulgate understand it in the latter sense. Some scholars connect this term with the identically spelled word כּפירים (“lions”) as a figurative description of princes or warriors (e.g., Pss 34:11; 35:17; 58:7; Jer 2:15; Ezek 32:2, 13; Nah 2:14; see HALOT 493 s.v.): “let us meet together with the leaders in the plain of Ono.”

rashi.heb:
*בכפירים.* 
שם מקום הוא:
rashi.eng: *in Kefirim.* This is a name of a place.

rashi.heb:
*בבקעת אונו.* 
כך שם הבקעה:
rashi.eng: *[which is] in the Valley of Ono.* That is the name of the valley.

rashi.heb:
*והמה חושבים.* 
הבנתי מהם שהיו חושבים עלי להרגני שם:
rashi.eng: *and they were plotting.* against me. I understood from them that they were plotting against me to assassinate me there.

rashi.heb:
*מלאכה גדולה אני עושה.* 
מבנייני (העיר ס"א) העפר:
rashi.eng: *"I am doing great work.* of the buildings (of the city); other editions read: [of the buildings] of dust.

rashi.heb:
*למה תשבת.* 
למה תהיה המלאכה בטלה:
rashi.eng: *Why should… stop.* Why should the work be curtailed?

rashi.heb:
*כאשר ארפה.* 
ידי מן הבניין:
rashi.eng: *when I leave it.* Heb. אַרְפֶּהָ, lit. [slacken] my hand from the building.

rashi.heb:
*וירדתי אליכם.* 
לדבר ולהועד אליכם:
rashi.eng: *and come down to you.* to speak with and to meet with you.

notes.151: (tn, Heb): “and I answered them according to this word.”

rashi.heb:
*את נערו.* 
ע"י נערו:
rashi.eng: *with his servant.* through his servant.

rashi.heb:
*ואגרת פתוחה בידו.* 
כתב אגרת שלח לי על ידו:
rashi.eng: *and an open letter was in his hand.* He sent me a written letter through him.

notes.153: (tn, Heb): “Gashmu”; in Neh 2:19 this name appears as Geshem. Since it is important for the modern reader to recognize that this is the same individual, the form of the name used here in the translation is the same as that in v. 19.

rashi.heb:
*כתוב בה.* 
באותה אגרת:
rashi.eng: *It was written in it.* in that letter.

rashi.heb:
*בגוים נשמע.* 
שנודע לכל העכו"ם שאתה וכל היהודים חושבים למרוד:
rashi.eng: *It is heard among the nations.* that it is known to all the nations that you and all the Jews are plotting to rebel.

rashi.heb:
*וגשמו אומר.* 
גשמו הוא גשם הערבי ופתרונו כאדם שאומר לחבירו כך הוא הדבר ופלוני אומר:
rashi.eng: *and Gashmu says.* Gashmu is Geshem the Arab, and its interpretation is like a man who says to his friend, “This is the matter, and so-and-so says.”

rashi.heb:
*כדברים האלה.* 
מוסב על כתוב בה ומקרא מסורס הוא והרי הוא כאילו נאמר כתוב בה כדברים האלה בגוים נשמע וגו':
rashi.eng: *according to these words.* This refers back to the text, and it is a transposed verse. It is as though it was written, “According to these words was heard among the nations, etc.”

notes.157: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*וגם נביאים וגו'.* 
עד ונועצה יחדיו היה כתוב באגרת:
rashi.eng: *… also… speakers.* Until “… and take counsel together” was written in the letter.

rashi.heb:
*נביאים.* 
בעלי לשון כמו בורא ניב שפתים (ישעיה ט'):
rashi.eng: *speakers.* Heb. נְבִיאִים, speakers, like (Isa. 57:19): “I created the speech (נִיב) of the lips.”

rashi.heb:
*לאמר.* 
שאומרים יש מלך ביהודה:
rashi.eng: *saying.* who say that there is a king in Judea.

rashi.heb:
*ועתה ישמע למלך.* 
אחרי שנקראת מלך ישמע למלך כדברים האלה:
rashi.eng: *and now it will be reported to the king.* After you have been called king, it will be reported to the king according to these words.

notes.159: (tn, Heb): “We are not according to these matters that you are saying.”
notes.160: (tn, Heb): “For from your heart you are inventing them.”

rashi.heb:
*כי מלבך.* 
הרי כי במקום אלא:
rashi.eng: *from your heart.* Heb. כִּי. This כִּי is in place of אֶלָּא, but.

rashi.heb:
*בודם.* 
קונטרבנטאל"ש בלע"ז כמו אשר בדה מלבו:
rashi.eng: *invent them.* contro(u)ves eles in Old French; you are concocting them, like (I Kings 12:33): “… that he had fabricated (בָּדָה) from his heart.”

notes.161: (tn): The participle has a desiderative nuance here, describing the desire of the subject and not necessarily the actual outcome. See also v. 14.
notes.162: (tn): The statement “So now, strengthen my hands” is frequently understood as an implied prayer, but is taken differently by NAB (“But instead, I now redoubled my efforts”).

rashi.heb:
*כי כולם.* 
כי כל העכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *For they all.* for all the nations.

rashi.heb:
*מיראים אותנו.* 
מתיראים ממנו וכך הם אומרים ירפו ידיהם וגו':
rashi.eng: *fear us.* Heb. מְיָרְאִים. They fear us, and so they say, “Let their hands be slackened, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*ועתה חזק את ידי.* 
לסייעני בבנין החומה:
rashi.eng: *and now, strengthen my hands.* to help me with the building of the wall.

notes.163: (tn, Heb): “shut in.” The reason for his confinement is not stated. BDB 783 s.v. עָצַר suggests that it had to do with the fulfillment of a vow or was related to an issue of ceremonial uncleanness.

rashi.heb:
*והוא עצור.* 
שמצאו בביתו:
rashi.eng: *and he was confined.* for he found him at home.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמר נועד.* 
אותו שמעיה היה נביא שקר וקבל שוחד מן סנבלט וחביריו להפחיד את נחמיה כדי לבטל את המלאכה:
rashi.eng: *and he said, "Let us meet.* Shemaiah was a false prophet who had received a bribe from Sanballat and his colleagues to frighten Nehemiah in order to stop the work.

rashi.heb:
*כי באים להרגך.* 
שהרי יבואו להרגך סנבלט וחביריו:
rashi.eng: *for they are coming to assassinate you.* for Sanballat and his colleagues will come to assassinate you.

rashi.heb:
*ולילה באים.* 
וע"כ הזהירו ליכנס בהיכל ולסגור הדלתות עליו שעדיין לא נעשו דלתות שערי העיר כמה שנאמר בתחילת הפרשה גם עד העת ההיא דלתות לא העמדתי בשערים:
rashi.eng: *and tonight they are coming.* Therefore, he warned him to enter the Temple and to close the doors about himself, because the doors of the gates of the city had not been made, as it says at the beginning of the chapter (verse 1): “Also that until that time, I had not erected doors in the gates.”

notes.164: (tn, Heb): “go into the temple and live.”

rashi.heb:
*האיש כמוני יברח.* 
בתמיה אם איש כמוני יברח ליכנס בהיכל:
rashi.eng: *Will a man like me flee.* This is a question: Will a man like me flee to enter the Temple?

rashi.heb:
*לא אבוא.* 
לא אכנס שם מפני פחד המיתה ולא אעבור על המצוה של הקב"ה שלא יבוא ויכנס זר בהיכלו:
rashi.eng: *I will not enter.* I will not enter there because of fear of death, and I will not transgress the commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He, that a stranger (a non-Kohen) may not enter His Temple.

notes.165: (tn, Heb): “and Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.”

rashi.heb:
*ואכירה.* 
הכרתי בדבריו שלא שלחו הקב"ה בדבר זה שאעבור עבירה מפני פחד המיתה:
rashi.eng: *And I discerned.* I discerned in his words that the Holy One, blessed be He, had not sent him on this mission, but that he wanted me to commit a transgression because of fear of death.

rashi.heb:
*כי הנבואה דבר עלי.* 
שהרי הוא דבר הדברים הללו עלי בשם נבואה:
rashi.eng: *for he spoke prophesy concerning me.* for he spoke these words concerning me in the name of prophecy.

rashi.heb:
*שכרו.* 
כל א' וא' מהם שכרו ונתנו לו שכר להפחידני ולבטל בבנין החומה:
rashi.eng: *had hired him.* Heb. שְּׂכָרוֹ. Each one of them had hired him and given him pay to frighten me and to curtail the building of the wall.

notes.166: (tc): The translation reads לִי (li, “to me”) rather than the MT reading לָהֶם (lahem, “to them”).

rashi.heb:
*למען שכור הוא.* 
אמר לי הדברים הללו:
rashi.eng: *Because he was hired.* he told me these things.

rashi.heb:
*למען אירא.* 
כדי שאתירא מהם להיות עושה כן ליכנס בהיכל ולהיות חוטא:
rashi.eng: *in order that I fear.* in order that I fear them, to do this to enter the Temple and sin.

rashi.heb:
*והיה להם לשם רע.* 
למען שיהיה להם לשם רע לחרפני בעבירה זו:
rashi.eng: *so that they should have this for a scandal.* in order that they should have this as a scandal to reproach me with this sin.

rashi.heb:
*וגם לנועדיה הנביאה.* 
היא ושאר נביאי השקר קבלו שכר מסנבלט וחביריו כדי להפחידני בנבואת שקריהם:
rashi.eng: *and also Noadiah the prophetess.* She and the rest of the false prophets received pay from Sanballat and his cohorts in order to frighten me with their false prophecies.

rashi.heb:
*בעשרים וחמשה.* 
ימים לחדש אלול בשנת כ' לדריוש המלך שבשנת עשרים לדריוש עלה נחמיה מבבל ובאותה שנה בנה חרבות ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *on the twenty-fifth.* day of the month of Ellul, in the twentieth year of King Darius, for in the twentieth year of Darius, Nehemiah went up from Babylon, and in that year he built the ruins of Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*לחמשים ושנים יום.* 
סוף נ"ב יום מיום שהתחילו לבנותו נגמר בנין החומה:
rashi.eng: *after fifty-two days.* The construction of the wall was completed fifty-two days after they had started building it.

notes.168: (tc): The MT understands the root here to be יָרֵא (yare’, “to fear”) rather than רָאָה (ra’ah, “to see”).
notes.169: (tn, Heb): “they greatly fell [i.e., were cast down] in their own eyes.” Some scholars suggest emending the reading of the MT, וַיִּפְּלוּ (vayyip�lu) to וַיִּפָּלֵא (vayyippale’, “it was very extraordinary in their eyes”).

rashi.heb:
*ויהי כאשר שמעו כל אויבינו.* 
דבר זה שנשלם בנין החומה:
rashi.eng: *Now it came to pass when all our enemies heard.* this matter, that the construction of the wall was completed.

rashi.heb:
*ויראו כל הגוים.* 
וכאשר ראו כל העכו"ם שנגמר בנין חומת העיר:
rashi.eng: *that all the nations became frightened.* when all the nations saw that the construction of the wall of the city had been completed.

rashi.heb:
*ויפלו מאד בעיניהם.* 
נפלו הם עצמם בעיניהם שהיו מואסים בעצמם כי נפל פחד היהודים עליהם:
rashi.eng: *and they fell very low in their own eyes.* They themselves fell in their own eyes; they despised themselves, for the fear of the Jews had fallen upon them.

rashi.heb:
*חורי יהודה.* 
שרי יהודה:
