rashi.eng: *the rulers of Judea.* Heb. חֹרֵי, the princes of Judea.

rashi.heb:
*על טוביה.* 
אל טוביה ישראל רשע היה, (עיין במס' קדושין ע, שמבואר שם שהיה עכו"ם וצ"ע מיוש"ה):
rashi.eng: *to Tobiah.* Heb. עַל-טוֹבִיָה. He was a renegade Israelite.

rashi.heb:
*ואשר לטוביה.* 
ואגרת אשר לטוביה:
rashi.eng: *and Tobiah’s.* i.e., Tobiah’s letters.

rashi.heb:
*כי רבים ביהודה.* 
שהיו שרים רבים ביהודה אשר היו לו לטוביה בעלי ברית ושבועה:
rashi.eng: *For many in Judea.* Heb. רַבִּים, who were great rulers in Judea, were partners in a covenant and an oath with him.

rashi.heb:
*כי חתן הוא.* 
אותו טוביה לשכניה:
rashi.eng: *for he was the son-in-law.* Tobiah [was the son-in-law] of Shechaniah.

rashi.heb:
*ויהוחנן בנו.* 
של טוביה:
rashi.eng: *and Jehohanan his son.* [the son] of Tobiah.

rashi.heb:
*בת משולם.* 
אותו משולם שר וגדול היה:
rashi.eng: *the daughter of Meshullam.* Meshullam was a great man and a ruler.

rashi.heb:
*גם טובותיו.* 
של טוביה היו מספרים לפני אותן בעלי שבועתו וקרוביו:
rashi.eng: *also of his good qualities.* His confederates and his kinsmen would speak of them before me.

rashi.heb:
*טובותיו.* 
ששפרואוצ"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *his good qualities.* Heb. טוֹבֹתָיו ses proezes, in Old French, his gallant exploits.

rashi.heb:
*היו מוציאים לו.* 
להגיד לו לטוביה:
rashi.eng: *they divulged to him.* to tell Tobiah.

rashi.heb:
*אגרת שלח טוביה.* 
אגרות היה שולח תדיר להפחידני שלא לבנות בנין החומ':
rashi.eng: *Tobiah sent letters.* He constantly sent letters to frighten me so that we would not build the wall.

rashi.heb:
*ויפקדו.* 
עתה נעשו הלוים פקודים על פקידותן להיותן שוערים ומשוררים מן הלוים בב"ה:
rashi.eng: *were appointed.* The Levites were now made appointees over their stations to be gatekeepers and singers in the Temple.

notes.173: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.174: (tn): Some have suggested that “Hananiah” is another name for Hanani, Nehemiah’s brother, so that only one individual is mentioned here. However, the third person plural in v. 3 indicates two people are in view.

rashi.heb:
*על ירושלים.* 
לשמור שערי ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *over Jerusalem.* to guard the gates of Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*מרבים.* 
מימים רבים:
rashi.eng: *for a long time.* Heb. מֵרַבִּים, lit. from many; from many days.

notes.175: (tc): The present translation (along with most English versions) reads with the Qere, a Qumran text, and the ancient versions וָאֹמַר (va’omar, “and I said”) rather than the Kethib of the MT, which reads וַיֹּאמֶר (vayyo’mer, “and he said”).
notes.176: (tn, Heb): “until the heat of the sun.” The phrase probably means that the gates were to be opened only after the day had progressed a bit, not at the first sign of morning light (cf. KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, TEV, CEV). It is possible, however, that the Hebrew preposition עַד (’ad), here translated as “until,” has a more rare sense of “during.” If so, this would mean that the gates were not to be left open and unattended during the hot part of the day when people typically would be at rest (cf. NLT).
notes.177: (tn): Presumably this would mean the gates were not to be opened until later in the morning and were to remain open until evening. Some, however, have understood Nehemiah’s instructions to mean that the gates were not to be left open during the hottest part of the day, but must be shut and locked while the guards are still on duty. See J. Barr, “Hebrew עַד, especially at Job i.18 and Neh vii.3,” JJS 27 (1982): 177-88.

rashi.heb:
*עד חום השמש.* 
עד חצי היום שהיה היום גדול:
rashi.eng: *until the sun becomes hot.* until midday, for the day was long.

rashi.heb:
*ועד הם עומדים.* 
ובעוד שהשערים פתוחים יהיו עומדים שלא יזוזו עד יגיפו ויסגרו הדלתות והרוצה לצאת יצא מן העיר והרוצה ליכנס יבא ויכנס כל כך היו עושים מפני האויבים:
rashi.eng: *and they shall stand until.* And as long as the doors are open, they shall stand; they shall not move until the doors are locked shut, and whoever wishes to leave may leave the city, and whoever wishes to enter may come and enter. They did all this because of the enemies.

rashi.heb:
*ואחוזו.* 
יאחזו הדלתות לסוגרם:
rashi.eng: *and hold them.* They should hold the doors to lock them.

rashi.heb:
*משמרות יושבי ירושלים.* 
מיושבי ירושלים העמידו משמרות גיט"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *watches among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.* of the inhabitants of Jerusalem station watches, jetes in Old French, (groups of) watchmen.

notes.179: (tn, Heb): “the people were few in its midst.”

rashi.heb:
*רחבת ידים.* 
רחבת מקום וגדולה:
rashi.eng: *a wide place.* Heb. רַחֲבַת יָדַיִם, a wide and large place.

notes.182: (tn, Heb): “in it”; the referent (the genealogical record) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*להתייחש.* 
לחקור יחוסן:
rashi.eng: *to trace their lineage.* Heb. לְהִתְיַחֵישׂ, to search for their lineage.

rashi.heb:
*העולים בראשונה.* 
מאותן היהודים העולים עם עזרא בראשונה:
rashi.eng: *those who went up at first.* of those Jews who went up with Ezra at first.

rashi.heb:
*ואמצא כתוב בו.* 
כל אלה הדברים היו כתובים באותה אגרת:
rashi.eng: *and I found written in it.* All these words were written in that letter.

notes.183: (tn, Heb): “the sons of”; KJV, ASV “the children of”; NAB “the inhabitants of.”
notes.185: (tc): One medieval Hebrew manuscript has “to Babylon.” Cf. Ezra 2:1.

rashi.heb:
*אלה בני המדינה וגו'.* 
עד והגורלות הפלנו על קרבן העצים (לקמן י' ל"ה):
rashi.eng: *These are the people of the province, etc..* until (10:35): “And we cast lots for the wood sacrifice.”

rashi.heb:
*וליהודה.* 
למדינת יהודה:
rashi.eng: *and to Judea.* to the province of Judea.

rashi.heb:
*איש לעירו.* 
כל א' לעירו:
rashi.eng: *each one to his city.* lit. a man to his city.

notes.186: (tn, Heb): “the men of the people of Israel.” Some English versions translate as “the people from Israel” (NCV) or “the Israelite people” (NRSV), but “men” should be retained because the following numbers presumably include only adult males.

rashi.heb:
*הבאים עם זרובבל.* 
אשר באו משבי הגולה עם זרובבל:
rashi.eng: *who came with Zerubbabel.* who came from the captivity of the exile with Zerubbabel.

rashi.heb:
*ישוע.* 
הוא יהושע בן יהוצדק הכהן הגדול חשבונות הללו פעמים הם מכוונים עם חשבונות של מעלה פעמים יש שאינם מכוונים זה כנגד זה ולא דקדק המקרא בחשבונות כל כך אבל הכלל שוה (עיין בעזרא סי' ב' פ"ב וצ"ע יוש"ה) לכאן ולכאן שנאמר כל הקהל כאחד וגו' ועל זה הכלל סמך כותב הספר ולא דקדק בחשבון הפרטיות כל כך והכל מפורש למעלה:

notes.213: (tn): The exact meaning of the pual participle מְפֹרָשׁ (m�forash) in this verse is uncertain. The basic sense of the Hebrew word seems to be “to make distinct.” The word may also have the sense of “to divide in parts,” “to interpret,” or “to translate.” The context of Neh 8:8 does not decisively clarify how the participle is to be understood here. It probably refers to the role of the Levites as those who explained or interpreted the portions of biblical text that had been publicly read on this occasion. A different option, however, is suggested by the translation distincte (“distinctly”) of the Vulgate (cf. KJV, ASV). If the Hebrew word means “distinctly” here, it would imply that the readers paid particular attention to such things as word-grouping and pronunciation so as to be sure that the listeners had every opportunity to understand the message that was being read. Yet another view is found in the Talmud, which understands translation of the Hebrew text into Aramaic to be what is in view here. The following explanation of Neh 8:8 is found in b. Megillah 3a: “‘And they read in the book, in the law of God’: this indicates the [Hebrew] text; ‘with an interpretation’: this indicates the targum; ‘and they gave the sense’: this indicates the verse stops; ‘and caused them to understand the reading’: this indicates the accentuation, or, according to another version, the Masoretic notes.” However, this ancient rabbinic view that the origins of the Targum are found in Neh 8:8 is debatable. It is not clear that the practice of paraphrasing the Hebrew biblical text into Aramaic in order to accommodate the needs of those Jews who were not at home in the Hebrew language developed this early. The translation of מְפֹרָשׁ adopted above (i.e., “explaining it”) understands the word to have in mind an explanatory function (cf. NAB, NCV, TEV, NLT) rather than one of translation.

notes.291: (tn, Heb): “from the peoples of the lands.” Cf. vv. 30, 31.

notes.293: (tn): The expression “a curse and an oath” may be a hendiadys, meaning “an oath with penalties.”
notes.295: (tn, Heb): “keep.” See the note on the word “obey” in Neh 1:5.
notes.296: (tn): The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here is אֲדֹנָי (’adonay).

rashi.heb:
*וכל הנבדל.* 
הם הגרים שנבדלו מתורת העכו"ם להיות דבוקים ומחוברים אל תורתו של הקדוש ברוך הוא ולשמור מצותיו:
rashi.eng: *and all who separated themselves.* These are the proselytes who separated themselves from the practice of the nations to cling and attach themselves to the Law of the Holy One, blessed be He, and to keep His commandments.

rashi.heb:
*על אחיהם.* 
עם אחיהם:
rashi.eng: *with their brethen.* Heb. עַל אֲחֵיהֶם with their brothers.

rashi.heb:
*אדיריהם.* 
גדולים שבהם:
rashi.eng: *their noblemen.* the great ones among them.

notes.298: (tn, Heb): “debt of every hand,” an idiom referring to the hand that holds legally binding contractual agreements.

notes.300: (tc): The MT reads “to give upon us.” However, the term עָלֵינוּ (’alenu, “upon us”) should probably be deleted, following a few medieval Hebrew MSS, the Syriac Peshitta, and the Vulgate.

rashi.heb:
*המקחות.* 
הסחורות:

*שבר.* 
תבואה כמו בשבר אשר הם שוברים (בראשית מ"ו):
rashi.eng: *and all grains.* Heb. שֶּׁבֶר, grain, like (Gen. 47:14): “… for the grain (בַּשֶּׁבֶר) that they were purchasing.”

rashi.heb:
*וביום קדש.* 
של י"ט:
rashi.eng: *or on holy days.* This refers to festivals.

rashi.heb:
*ונטוש את השנה השביעית.* 
כענין שנאמר והשביעית תשמטנה ונטשתה (שמות כג):
rashi.eng: *and we shall abandon during the seventh year.* As is stated (Exod. 23:11): “But throughout the seventh year you shall let it go and abandon it (וּנְטַשְּׁתָּה).”

rashi.heb:
*ומשא כל יד.* 
השמטת מלוה בשביעית:
rashi.eng: *and the loan given by every hand.* This refers to the release of loans during the seventh year.

rashi.heb:
*וכל מלאכת בית אלהינו.* 
לעשות מן הכסף:
rashi.eng: *and all the work of the Temple of our God.* to do with money.

notes.303: (tn): The words “we accept responsibility” are not included in the Hebrew text, but are inferred from v. 33 (so also in v. 37).

rashi.heb:
*הפלנו.* 
כמה יביא כל אחד:
rashi.eng: *we cast.* how much each one should bring.

rashi.heb:
*קרבן העצים.* 
תקרובת של עצי המערכה למזבח:
rashi.eng: *the wood offering.* an offering of wood for the arrangement on the altar.

rashi.heb:
*לבית אבותינו.* 
שהיא בית קדושת אבותינו:
rashi.eng: *to the House of our forefathers.* which is the House of the sanctity of our forefathers.

rashi.heb:
*ובכורי כל פרי כל עץ.* 
בכורי של כל פרי האילן הם מדברי חכמים:
rashi.eng: *the first fruits of our soil.* The first of every fruit of a tree. They are required by rabbinical injunction.

notes.306: (tn, Heb): “And the priest the son of Aaron.”

rashi.heb:
*נביא לכהנים אל לשכות.* 
כי שם היו רגילים:
rashi.eng: *we shall bring to the priests to the chambers.* for they were usually there.

rashi.heb:
*המעשרים בכל ערי עבודתנו.* 
שנוטלים מעשרותיה' בכל ערי ישראל:
rashi.eng: *who receive tithes in all the cities of our work.* who take their tithes in all the cities of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*בעשר.* 
ל' בעשור:
rashi.eng: *at the [Levites’] tithing.* Heb. בַּעְשֵּׂר;an expression meaning at the tithing.

rashi.heb:
*את מעשר המעשר.* 
שהיו הלוים מעשרים מעשר מן המעשר ומביאים אותו לכהנים שלא היו עוזבים את בית המקדש:
rashi.eng: *the tithe of the tithe.* for the Levites would take a tithe from the tithe and bring it up to the priests, who did not leave the Temple.

notes.307: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.308: (tn, Heb): “nine of the hands.” The word “hand” is used here in the sense or a part or portion.

rashi.heb:
*אחד מן העשרה.* 
שבישראל למען ישבו בירושלים לשמור העיר:
rashi.eng: *one of ten.* of Israel, so that they should dwell in Jerusalem to guard the city.

rashi.heb:
*ותשע הידות.* 
תשעה חלקים שבישראל:
rashi.eng: *and nine parts.* nine parts of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*המתנדבים.* 
אשר נדבה רוחם אותם להיות יושבים בירושלים לשמור העיר מן האויבים:
rashi.eng: *who volunteered.* whose spirit inspired them to volunteer to dwell in Jerusalem to guard the city from enemies.

rashi.heb:
*ואלה ראשי המדינה אשר ישבו בירושלים.* 
הוא שנאמר בסמוך ובירושלים ישבו בני יהודה וגו':
rashi.eng: *And these are the heads of the province who dwelt in Jerusalem.* these are the ones regarding whom it is stated below: “And in Jerusalem there dwelt of the children of Judah, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*מבני יהודה עתיה וגו'.* 
חוזר ומפרש מבני יהודה מי ומי היו וכל הפרשה אינה מונה כי אם הגדולים והחשובים שבהם:
rashi.eng: *of the children of Judah: Athaiah, etc..* He returns to explain who those ‘of the children of Judah’ were, and the entire chapter enumerates only the great and esteemed ones among them.

notes.310: (tc): The translation reads מִן־הַשֵּׁלָנִי (min hashelani, “from the Shelahite”) rather than the MT reading בֶּן־הַשִּׁלֹנִי (ben hashiloni, “the son of the Shilionite”). See 1 Chr 9:5.

notes.311: (tn, Heb): “those behind him.” Some scholars emend the text to וְאֶחָיו (v�’ekhayv, “his brothers”).

rashi.heb:
*פקיד.* 
ממונה:
rashi.eng: *the official.* the one appointed.

rashi.heb:
*משנה.* 
אחר (הפקיד):
rashi.eng: *the second in command.* after [the official].

rashi.heb:
*נגיד.* 
ממונה:
rashi.eng: *the official.* [as translated,] the official.

rashi.heb:
*נגיד בית האלהים.* 
ממונה על בית אלהים:
rashi.eng: *the official over the Temple of God.* appointed over the Temple of God.

rashi.heb:
*ואחיהם עושה המלאכה לבית.* 
וחבריהם שהיו עובדים עבודת הבית וקרבנותיו:
rashi.eng: *And their brethren who performed the work of the Temple.* and their colleagues, who were performing the service of the Temple and its sacrifices.

rashi.heb:
*ראשים לאבות.* 
ראשי בית אב ממשפחות הכהנים:
rashi.eng: *rulers over the fathers’ houses.* the heads of the fathers’ houses of the priestly families.

notes.314: (tc): The translation reads with the LXX וְאֶחָיו (v�’ekhayv, “and his brothers”) rather than the MT reading וַאֲחֵיהֶם (va’akhehem, “and their brothers”).

rashi.heb:
*ופקיד עליהם.* 
ממונה עליהם:
rashi.eng: *and the official over them.* the one appointed over them.

rashi.heb:
*על המלאכה החיצונה.* 
אשר לבית כגון בנייני בדק הבית ועצי המערכה שהיו מביאים מבחוץ:
rashi.eng: *over the outside work.* of the Temple, such as the buildings of the repair of the Temple (sic) and the wood of the arrangement, which they would bring from outside.

notes.316: (tc): The translation reads with the Lucianic Greek recension and Vulgate הַתְּהִלָה (hatt�hilah, “the praise”) rather than the MT reading הַתְּחִלָּה (hatt�khillah, “the beginning”).

rashi.heb:
*ראש התחלה יהודה לתפלה.* 
הוא היה ראש וממונ' וגדול לפתוח תחלה להודות בתפלה ובזמירות שירותיהם של לוים, יהודה כמו יודה והה"א נכנסת בתיבה שלא לצורך כמו יוסף יהוסף:
rashi.eng: *the head to begin the thanksgiving in prayer.* He was the head and the appointed official, and the greatest one who was first to start and to thank in prayer and in singing the songs of the Levites. יְהוֹדֶה is like יוֹדֶה, and the “hey” enters the word unnecessarily, like יוֹסֵף and יְהוֹסֵף.

rashi.heb:
*והשוערים.* 
ממונין על שערי המקדש:
rashi.eng: *And the gatekeepers.* those appointed over the gates of the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*איש בנחלתו.* 
כל אחד בנחלתו היו יושבים:
rashi.eng: *each one in his inheritance.* They were dwelling each one in his inheritance.

notes.317: (tn, Heb): “the temple attendants.” The pronoun “them” has been substituted in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*בעופל.* 
מקום אחד אשר בירושלים:
rashi.eng: *in the Ophel.* a place that was in Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*על הנתינים.* 
ממונים על הנתינים:
rashi.eng: *over the Nethinites.* appointed over the Nethinites.

rashi.heb:
*ופקיד הלוים.* 
ממונה על הלוים אשר בירושלים:
rashi.eng: *And the official over the Levites.* appointed over the Levites in Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*לנגד מלאכת.* 
על מלאכת הבית ממונה כגון בנייני בדק הבית ושאר דברים שמוציאין ממון למעשה (למעשר) הבית כענין שנאמר למעלה ושבתי ויוזבד על המלאכה החיצונה וגו':
rashi.eng: *over the work of the Temple of God.* He was appointed over the work of the Temple, such as the buildings of the repair of the Temple and the rest of the matters for which money is spent for the work of the Temple, like the matter that is stated above (verse 16): “… and Shabbethai and Jazabad over the outside work, etc.”

notes.318: (tn, Heb): “the commandment of the king was over them.”
notes.319: (tn, Heb): “a thing of a day in its day.”

rashi.heb:
*כי מצות המלך עליהם.* 
והמלך היה מאמין בהם:
rashi.eng: *For the command of the king was upon them and [his] trust.* The king trusted them.

rashi.heb:
*על המשוררים.* 
להוציא ממון מאוצר המלך דריוש:
rashi.eng: *upon the singers.* to spend money from King Darius’s treasury.

rashi.heb:
*דבר יום ביומו.* 
כדי לעשות צרכי הבית:
rashi.eng: *for the daily requirements.* in order to perform the requirements of the Temple.

notes.320: (tn, Heb): “to the hand of the king.”

rashi.heb:
*ליד המלך.* 
הוא היה מצרן לעצת המלך דריוש:
rashi.eng: *at the king’s hand.* He was privy to King Darius’s counsel.

rashi.heb:
*לכל דבר.* 
לכל דבריהם אשר לעם לדבר עליהם אל המלך:
rashi.eng: *for every matter.* for every matter that concerned the people, to speak to the king on their behalf.

notes.321: (tn, Heb): “its daughters.” So also in vv. 27, 28, 30, and 31.

notes.322: (tc): The translation reads with a few medieval Hebrew MSS and the Syriac Peshitta וּמִבְּנֵי (umibb�ney, “and some of the descendants of”; cf. NLT) rather than the MT reading וּבְנֵי (uv�ne, “and the sons of”).
notes.323: (tc, Heb): “from Geba.” It is preferable to delete the preposition “from” read by the MT.

notes.327: (tn, Heb): “Ge-harashim,” which could be left untranslated as a place name.

rashi.heb:
*מחלקות יהודה לבנימין.* 
היו מחלקין במחלקותם אנה ואנה בארץ יהודה ובנימין:
rashi.eng: *there were divisions to Judah and to Benjamin.* They were divided into their divisions here and there in the land of Judah and Benjamin.

rashi.heb:
*וישוע.* 
הוא יהושע הכהן הגדול:
rashi.eng: *and Jeshua.* That is Joshua the High Priest.

notes.329: (tc): Most Hebrew MSS read “Ginnethoi”; the present translation follows a number of Hebrew MSS and the Vulgate (cf. Neh 12:16 and NIV, NCV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*בימי ישוע.* 
שהיו ראשים בימי יהושע כהן גדול:
rashi.eng: *in the days of Jeshua.* i.e., those who were leaders in the days of Joshua the High Priest.

rashi.heb:
*הידות.* 
מן כלי שיר לומר שירה:
rashi.eng: *huyedoth.* [This was] a type of musical instrument which accompanied the songs.

notes.333: (tc): The translation reads וְעֻנִּי (v�’unni) with the Qere rather than וְעֻנּוֹ (v�’uno) of the MT Kethib.

rashi.heb:
*למשמרות.* 
כמו שמצינו (בדברי הימים א' כ"ד ואילך) שהלוים היו חלוקים לעשרים וארבעה משמרות:
rashi.eng: *in the watches.* as we find (in I Chronicles from ch. 24 on) that the Levites were divided into twenty-four watches.

rashi.heb:
*וישוע הוליד את יויקים וגו'.* 
כל אלו שבמקרא זה היו כהנים גדולים:
rashi.eng: *Now Jeshua begot Joiakim, etc..* All those [listed] in this verse were high priests.

rashi.heb:
*ובימי יויקים.* 
שהיה כהן גדול היו כהנים הללו הם היו ראשים ראשי בית אב למשמרותם:
rashi.eng: *And in the days of Joiakim.* who was the high priest. These priests were the leaders of the fathers’ houses of their watches.

rashi.heb:
*לשריה מריה.* 
למשמרת של שריה היה מריה ראש בית אב ולמשמרת של ירמיה היה חנניה ראש בית אב וכן כולם ואת אשר לא פירש כל העשרי' וארבע משמרות לא דקדק המקרא בכך למנותם כולם:
rashi.eng: *of Seraiah was Meraiah.* Of the watch of Seraiah, the head of the father’s house was Meraiah, and of the watch of Jeremiah, the head of the father’s house was Hananiah, and so it is with them all, and the reason Scripture did not list all twenty-four watches is that it is not exacting in enumerating them all.

notes.335: (tc): The present translation reads with the LXX לְמַלּוּךְ (l�mallukh) rather than לִמְלוּכִי (limlukhi) of the Kethib (by dittography) or לִמְלִיכוּ (limlikhu) of the Qere.
notes.336: (tc): Most Hebrew MSS read “Shebaniah” (cf. KJV, NAB, NASB, NRSV, CEV); the present translation follows the reading of some Hebrew MSS, some LXX MSS, and the Syriac (cf. Neh 12:3 and NIV, NCV, NLT).

notes.337: (tc): The present translation reads with the Lucianic Greek recension and the Syriac Peshitta לִמְרֵמוֹת (limremot, cf. NAB, NIV, NCV, NLT “Meremoth”) rather than the MT reading לִמְרָיוֹת (limrayot, cf. KJV, NASB, NRSV, CEV “Meraioth”). Cf. v. 3.

notes.338: (tc): The present translation (along with most English versions) reads with the Qere and the Syriac Peshitta לְעִדּוֹא (l�’iddo’, “Iddo”) rather than the MT reading לַעֲדָיָא (la’adaya’) which probably arose through graphic confusion. Cf. v. 4.

notes.339: (tn): Or “of Miniamin, …; of Moadiah, Piltai,” where the name of the leader of the family of Miniamin has dropped out of the text due to a problem in transmission.

notes.340: (tc): The present translation reads סַלּוּ (sallu, cf. NAB, NIV, NCV, NLT “Sallu”) rather than the MT reading סַלַּי (sallai, cf. KJV, NASB, NRSV, CEV “Sallai” ). Cf. v. 7.

notes.341: (tn): Some scholars delete these words, regarding them as a later scribal addition to the text.

rashi.heb:
*הלוים בימי אלישיב.* 
הלוים הללו היו ראשי בית אבות במשמרות הלוים בימי אלישיב הכהן הגדול והכהנים המנוין למעלה בסמוך הם היו ראשי בית אבות במשמרותם גם בימי אלישיב:
rashi.eng: *The Levites in the days of Eliashib.* These Levites were the heads of the fathers’ houses in the watches of the Levites in the days of Eliashib the High Priest, and the priests enumerated immediately above were the heads of the fathers’ houses in their watches, also in the days of Eliashib.

rashi.heb:
*על מלכות.* 
בימי מלכות דריוש היה דבר זה:
rashi.eng: *in the reign of.* This matter came about in the days of Darius.

notes.342: (tn): Or “the Book of the Annals” (so NRSV); NLT “The Book of History.”

rashi.heb:
*ועד ימי יוחנן.* 
כל אותן שהיו ראשי אבות הלוים עד ימי יוחנן כהן גדול מנוין שם בדברי הימים:
rashi.eng: *even until the days of Johanan.* All those who were the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Levites until the days of Johanan the High Priest were enumerated in the chronicles.

rashi.heb:
*משמר לעומת משמר.* 
שהיו חלוקים במשמרותם לומר שירה:
rashi.eng: *a watch opposite a watch.* for they were divided into their watches to recite the song.

rashi.heb:
*שוערים משמר.* 
שוערים היו במשמר שלהם לשמור שערי הבית:
rashi.eng: *sentries of the gates [in their] watch.* The sentries of the gates were in their watch to guard the gates of the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*באסופי.* 
כמו בסיפי השערים:
rashi.eng: *at the thresholds.* Heb. בַּאֲסֻפֵּי, like בְּסִיפֵּי הַשְּׁעָרִים, at the thresholds of the gates.

rashi.heb:
*אלה בימי יויקים.* 
אלה היו שוערים בימי יויקים:
rashi.eng: *These were in the days of Joiakim.* These were the gate sentries in the days of Joiakim.

notes.345: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.346: (tn, Heb): “from all their places.” The words “they lived” are implied.

rashi.heb:
*ובחנוכת חומת ירושלים.* 
בתשלום חומת העיר לקדש את העיר:
rashi.eng: *And in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.* at the completion of the wall of the city, to sanctify the city.

rashi.heb:
*ובתודות.* 
ובהודאות:
rashi.eng: *and with thanksgivings.* Heb. וּבְתוֹדוֹת, and with thanksgivings.

rashi.heb:
*ומן הככר.* 
אשר סביבות ירושלים באו המשוררים:
rashi.eng: *and from the plain.* the singers came from [the plain] surrounding Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*ויטהרו.* 
תחלה טהרו את עצמן ואח"כ טהרו את אחרים:
rashi.eng: *purified themselves.* First they purified themselves, and afterwards they purified the others.

rashi.heb:
*ואת השערים ואת החומה.* 
שלא תהיה טומאה שם בעיר:
rashi.eng: *and the gates and the wall.* that there should be no uncleanliness in the city.

notes.348: (tc): The translation reads וְהָאַחַת הֹלֶכֶת (v�ha’akhat holekhet, “and one was proceeding”) rather than the MT reading וְתַהֲלֻכֹת (v�tahalukhot, “and processions”).

rashi.heb:
*מעל לחומה.* 
שקדש את העיר והלכו השרים ובית דין והכהנים והלוים עם שתי תודות סביב לעיר הכל כמפורש במסכת שבועות כדי לקדש את העיר:
rashi.eng: *upon the wall.* meaning that he sanctified the city, the princes, the tribunal, and the Levites with two thanksgiving offerings around the city, as is delineated in Tractate Shebuoth (14a, 15a, b), in order to sanctify the city.

rashi.heb:
*שתי תודות.* 
שתי לחמי תודה כל לחם ולחם קרוי תודה:
rashi.eng: *two… thanksgiving offerings.* two breads of the thanksgiving offerings, each bread being called a thanksgiving offering.

rashi.heb:
*ותהלוכות לימין.* 
וכאשר יצאו מן העיר כדי לסובבה הלכו לצד ימינה:
rashi.eng: *with processions to the right.* And when they went out of the city in order to encompass it, they went to the right side.

rashi.heb:
*יהודה ובנימין.* 
שני שרים היו:
rashi.eng: *Judah and Benjamin.* They were two princes.

notes.349: (tn, Heb): “some of the sons of the priests.”

notes.350: (tn): Or “prescribed by” (NIV, NLT); TEV “of the kind played by.” The precise relationship of these musical instruments to David is not clear.

rashi.heb:
*ואחיו.* 
חביריו של זכריה הכהן:
rashi.eng: *And his brethren.* the colleagues of Zechariah the priest.

rashi.heb:
*ועל שער העין.* 
לפני שער העין הלכו סביבות העיר:
rashi.eng: *And by the Fountain Gate.* Before the Fountain Gate, they marched around the city.

rashi.heb:
*ונגדם עלו.* 
ולפניהם עלו משער העין למעלות של עיר דוד ואותן מעלות היו לחומה:
rashi.eng: *and opposite them.* And before them they ascended from the Fountain Gate to the steps of the City of David, and those steps led to the wall.

notes.352: (tc): The translation reads הוֹלֶכֶת (holekhet, “was proceeding”) rather than the MT הַהוֹלֶכֶת (haholekhet, “the one proceeding”). The MT probably reflects dittography – accidental writing of ה (hey) twice instead of once.

rashi.heb:
*והתודה השנית ההולכת למול.* 
תודה אחרת שהיתה שנית לחברתה היתה הולכת נגד חברתה בשוה ולא זו אחר זו:
rashi.eng: *And the second thanksgiving offering, which went opposite [it].* The other thanksgiving offering, which was second to its fellow, went opposite its fellow, alongside it, not one following the other.

rashi.heb:
*ואני אחריה.* 
ואני הייתי הולך אחריה של תודה:
rashi.eng: *and I was after it.* And I marched after it, [i.e.,] after the thanksgiving offering.

notes.353: (tn): Or “the Old Gate” (so KJV, NASB, NCV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*ועמדו.* 
שם היו עומדים שלא לילך יותר:
rashi.eng: *and they stood.* They stood, there and did not go any further.

rashi.heb:
*שתי התודות.* 
שנשאו אותם לבהמ"ק:
rashi.eng: *the two thanksgiving offerings.* that they carried to the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*בחצוצרות.* 
היו תוקעין מתוך שמחתן:
rashi.eng: *with the trumpets.* They sounded the trumpets out of their joy.

notes.357: (tc): The translation reads מִשְּׂדֶי (miss�de, “from the fields”) rather than the MT reading לִשְׂדֵי (lisdey, “to the fields”).
notes.358: (tn, Heb): “for Judah.” The words “the people of” have been supplied in the translation for clarity, since “Judah” is a proper name as well as a place name.

rashi.heb:
*ויפקדו.* 
לשון פקידות:
rashi.eng: *were appointed.* Heb. וַיִפָקְדוּ, a word meaning appointment.

rashi.heb:
*הנשכות.* 
כמו הלשכות של בית המקדש:
rashi.eng: *the chambers.* Heb. הַנְשָׁכוֹת, like הַלְשָּׁכוֹת, the chambers of the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*לכנוס בהם.* 
ובאותן הלשכות היו נותנים כל מתנותיהם של כהנים ולוים ומשם היו חולקין ביניהם:
rashi.eng: *to gather in them.* And in these chambers they would place all the gifts of the priests and the Levites, and from there they would distribute [them] among them.

rashi.heb:
*מנאות.* 
כמו מנות:
rashi.eng: *portions.* Heb. מְנָאוֹת like מָנוֹת.

rashi.heb:
*לכהנים ללוים.* 
כהנים היו נוטלים הראוי להם והלוים הראוי להם:
rashi.eng: *for the priests and for the Levites.* The priests were taking what was due them and the Levites what was due them.

rashi.heb:
*העומדים.* 
ומשמשים שם לפני הקב"ה בתודות והודאות:
rashi.eng: *who stood.* and ministered there before the Holy One, blessed be He, with thanksgiving offerings and thanksgivings.

notes.360: (tc): With many medieval Hebrew MSS and the ancient versions the translation reads the conjunction (“and”). It is absent in the Leningrad MS that forms the textual basis for BHS.

notes.361: (tn, Heb): “heads.” The translation reads with the Qere the plural רֹאשֵׁי (ro’shey, “heads”) rather than the Kethib singular רֹאשׁ (ro’sh, “head”) of the MT.

notes.362: (tn, Heb): “a thing of a day in its day.”

rashi.heb:
*מניות.* 
כמו מנות:
rashi.eng: *the portions.* Heb. מְנָיוֹת, like מָנוֹת.

rashi.heb:
*ומקדישים ללוים.* 
היו נותנים במעשר ללוים והם היו נוטלים מעשר מן המעשר ונותנים לכהנים:
rashi.eng: *and they consecrated [them] for the Levites.* And they would give the tithe to the Levites, who would take the tithe from the tithe and give it to the priests.

notes.365: (tn, Heb): “it was found.” The Hebrew verb is passive.

notes.366: (tn, Heb): “bread.” The Hebrew term is generic here, however, referring to more than bread alone.

rashi.heb:
*כל ערב.* 
כל תערובות העכו"ם כמו וגם ערב רב עלה אתם (שמות י״ב:ל״ח):
rashi.eng: *all mixtures.* Every mixture of heathens, like (Exodus 12:38): “A great mixed multitude (עֵרֶב רַב) also went up with them.”

notes.367: (tc): The translation reads the plural rather than the singular of the MT.

rashi.heb:
*ולפני מזה.* 
ומקודם לכן:
rashi.eng: *Now prior to this.* Heb. וְלִפְנֵי מִזֶה, before this.

rashi.heb:
*קרוב לטוביה.* 
אותו אלישיב הכהן היה קרוב לטוביה חברו של סנבלט ונתן שם הכהן כליו של טוביה:
rashi.eng: *was a kinsman of Tobiah.* Eliashib the priest was a kinsman of Tobiah the companion of Sanballat, and the priest placed Tobiah’s vessels there.

rashi.heb:
*ויעש.* 
אלישיב:
rashi.eng: *And he made.* Eliashib [made].

rashi.heb:
*לפנים.* 
שם היו נותנים קודם שבאתי לירושלים:
rashi.eng: *in previous times.* Before I came to Jerusalem, they would put [them] there.

rashi.heb:
*מצות הלוים.* 
מתנות הראויות ללוים:
rashi.eng: *which were ordained for the Levites.* the gifts due the Levites.

notes.369: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*ובכל זה.* 
ובכל המעשה הזה:
rashi.eng: *Now with all this.* during this entire episode.

rashi.heb:
*באתי אל המלך.* 
וחזרתי לבבל:
rashi.eng: *I came to the king.* when I returned to Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*נשאלתי.* 
שיתן לי רשות לעלות לירושלים ולחזור:
rashi.eng: *I requested of the king.* to give me permission to go up and to return to Jerusalem.

notes.371: (tn): On the usage of this Hebrew word see HALOT 478-79 s.v. כְּלִי.

rashi.heb:
*ואומרה.* 
צויתי לטהר ויטהרו הלשכות וגומר:
rashi.eng: *And I commanded.* I commanded to purify it, and they purified the chambers, etc.

rashi.heb:
*מניות.* 
מנות:
rashi.eng: *portions.* Heb. מְנָיוֹת, [like] מָנוֹת.

rashi.heb:
*לא נתנה.* 
שלא נתנו ישראל שם המתנות ועל כן ברחו והלכו להם אנה ואנה לשאול מתנותיהם ולא היו עוסקים כל כך בעבודתם:
rashi.eng: *had not been given.* that the Israelites had not placed the gifts there, and because of that they fled and wandered here and there to ask for their gifts, and were not occupied as much with their service.

notes.372: (tn, Heb): “and I stood them on their standing.”

rashi.heb:
*ואקבצם.* 
קבצתי את הכהנים והלוים להעמידם על משמרתם בעבודתם וכל ישראל היו מביאים להם שם מתנותם:
rashi.eng: *And I gathered them.* I gathered the priests and the Levites to station them on their watches in their service, and all of Israel brought them their gifts there.

notes.373: (tc): Probably one should read with the Lucianic Greek recension, the Syriac Peshitta, and the Vulgate וָאֲצַוֶּה (va’atsavveh, “and I commanded”) rather than the rare denominative verb וָאוֹצְרָה (va’ots�rah, “and I appointed over the storeroom”) of the MT.

rashi.heb:
*כי נאמנים.* 
היו לחלוק המתנות ביניהם:
rashi.eng: *for they were deemed trustworthy.* to distribute the gifts among them [the Levites].

rashi.heb:
*הערמות.* 
אלומות של תבואה:
rashi.eng: *the stacks.* sheaves of grain.

rashi.heb:
*ואעיד.* 
העידותי בהם שלא לעשות:
rashi.eng: *and I warned.* I warned them not to do it.

rashi.heb:
*ביום מכרם ציד.* 
ביום שהיו מוכרים מזון וציד, ציד כמו ויתן להם צידה לדרך (בראשית מ"ח):
rashi.eng: *on the day they sold provisions.* On the day they were selling food and provisions. צָיִד, provisions, as (Gen. 45:21): “… and he gave them provision (צֵדָה) for the way.”

notes.377: (map): For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.
notes.378: (tn): The words “of all places” are not in the Hebrew text but have been supplied in the translation to indicate the emphasis on Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*והצורים.* 
סוחרים של צור מביאים דגים למכור:
rashi.eng: *and the Tyrian.* Merchants of Tyre would bring fish to sell.

notes.380: (tn, Heb): “the gates of Jerusalem grew dark.”

rashi.heb:
*ויהי כאשר צללו.* 
כאשר נטו הצללים של ערב שבת בשערים צויתי לסגור דלתות העיר שלא יפתחו עד אחר שבת שלא יבואו הרוכלים בעיר למכור סחורתן כדי שלא יחללו ישראל את השבת על ידיהם:
rashi.eng: *Now it came to pass when the gates of Jerusalem cast shadows.* When the shadows of the Sabbath eve fell on the gates, I ordered the doors of the city to be closed and not re-opened until after the Sabbath so that the traffickers would not enter the city to sell their merchandise and cause Israel to profane the Sabbath.

rashi.heb:
*וילינו.* 
והיו לנים הרוכלים והסוחרים ביום השבת מחוץ לירושלים פעם א' ושתי פעמים כדי שיבואו בני ישראל לפתוח השערים ולקנות מהם בשבת:
rashi.eng: *So… lodged.* The traffickers and the merchants lodged outside Jerusalem on the Sabbath once and twice so that the Children of Israel would open the gates and buy from them on the Sabbath.

notes.383: (tn): The Hebrew text includes the words “to them,” but they have been excluded from the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.384: (tn, Heb): “I will send a hand on you.”
notes.385: (sn): This statement contains a great deal of restrained humor. The author clearly takes pleasure in the effectiveness of the measures that he had enacted.

rashi.heb:
*ואומרה אליהם.* 
התריתי באותם הרוכלים:
rashi.eng: *and I said to them.* I warned those traffickers.

rashi.heb:
*אם תשנו.* 
אם תוסיפו לעשות פעם שנייה:
rashi.eng: *If you repeat this.* if you continue to do this a second time.

rashi.heb:
*מן העת.* 
מן אותו יום והלאה לא באו ביום השבת:
rashi.eng: *Since that time.* From that day on, they did not come on the Sabbath day.

rashi.heb:
*הושיבו נשים.* 
אשר נשאו להם נשים של עכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *who had married.* who had married heathen wives.

rashi.heb:
*חצי מדבר.* 
הרבה מבניהם היו מדברים לשון אשדודי' כאמותם:
rashi.eng: *And half… were speaking.* Many of their children spoke the Ashdodite language like their mothers.

rashi.heb:
*ואכה.* 
נתתי להם מלקיות להלקותם כדי להוכיחם ולהזכירם:
rashi.eng: *and I struck.* I gave them lashes in order to chastise them and remind them.

rashi.heb:
*גם אותו החטיאו.* 
כל שכן שתהיו חוטאים ע"י נשיכם של עכו"ם וזהו שנאמר בסמוך ולכם הנשמע וגו' בתמיה כלומר שלמה מלך ישראל נמצא חטא על ידי נשי' של עכו"ם ואתם נשאתם נשים של עכו"ם להיות חוטאין:
rashi.eng: *caused him even to sin.* If he sinned, how much more so is it certain that you will sin through your heathen wives! As is written in the next verse, “Shall we hearken, etc.?” i.e., Solomon was found sinning through his heathen wives, and you have married foreign wives in order to sin?

rashi.heb:
*ומבני יוידע.* 
חתן לסנבלט אחד מבני יוידע חתן לסנבלט צורר היהודים והברחתיהו מעלי למען לא יהיה רגיל בירושלים בשביל חתנו לראות את העיר ואת מוצאיה ואת מובאיה:
rashi.eng: *And [one] of the sons of Joiada… was the son in law of Sanballat.* One of the sons of Joiada was the son-in-law of Sanballat, the adversary of the Jews; thus, I drove him away from me so that he should not frequent Jerusalem because of his son-in-law, to see the city and the ways to enter and leave it.

notes.390: (tc): One medieval Hebrew MS, the Lucianic Greek recension, and the Syriac Peshitta read the plural הַכֹּהֲנִים (hakkohanim, “the priests”) rather than the singular reading of the MT, הַכְּהֻנָּה (hakk�hunnah, “the priesthood”).

rashi.heb:
*זכרה להם.* 
הטובה אשר עשו:
rashi.eng: *Remember them.* the good that they did.

notes.392: (tn): The words “I also provided for” are not included in the Hebrew text, but are supplied in the translation for the sake of clarity.

rashi.heb:
*בעתים.* 
לעתים היו כורתים עצים למערכה:
rashi.eng: *at appointed times.* They would cut wood for the altar pyre at appointed times.
*and concerning the first fruits.* that they should bring the first fruits at a certain time; for each species I appointed its time.
